additions.l4: Reserve setting and reserve adequacy review
additions.name: Issue Statement of Actuarial Opinion
additions.description: Appointed Actuary prepares and signs the annual Statement of Actuarial Opinion on reserves, plus the supporting Actuarial Report and confidential Actuarial Opinion Summary, for inclusion with the statutory Annual Statement and Board notification per NAIC Annual Statement Instructions.
additions.supporting: Reserving Actuary, Chief Actuary, Statutory Reporting Manager
additions.inputs: Booked reserves, reserve report, actuarial workpapers, NAIC Annual Statement Instructions, Board appointment record
additions.outputs: Signed Statement of Actuarial Opinion, Actuarial Opinion Summary, Actuarial Report, Board/regulator notifications
additions.deliverable: Statement of Actuarial Opinion (with Actuarial Opinion Summary)
additions.rationale: Every U.S. insurer must file an annual SAO signed by a Board-appointed Appointed Actuary with its Annual Statement (NAIC Annual Statement Instructions; Model #745). Verified: RF-21-02 ends at S06 'Book Reserves' with no opinion step, and no SAO/actuarial-opinion step exists in any of the 29 streams — Finance's F-11-01-S06 ('File Regulatory Reports') submits statutory filings but nothing produces the actuarial opinion that must accompany them. A regulator or Appointed Actuary would immediately flag its absence.

additions.name: Calculate Life & Annuity Statutory Reserves
additions.description: Run the periodic statutory valuation of life and annuity liabilities under the NAIC Valuation Manual — VM-20 principle-based reserves for life (NPR/deterministic/stochastic), VM-21 for variable annuities — including assumption governance, model runs, exclusion tests and VM-31 PBR Actuarial Report exhibits.
additions.supporting: ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary, Actuarial Analyst, Chief Actuary
additions.inputs: Policy inforce extracts, mortality/lapse/expense assumptions, economic scenarios, NAIC Valuation Manual (VM-20/VM-21) requirements
additions.outputs: Life & annuity statutory reserves, PBR exhibits, VM-31 report inputs
additions.deliverable: Life & annuity statutory reserve valuation (PBR results)
additions.rationale: Meridian is a combined P&C + Life & Retirement insurer, but the entire Reserving L4 (RF-21-02) is built on P&C claims triangles (claims data extracts, development patterns). Verified: no PBR, VM-20/VM-21, Valuation Manual, or life/annuity statutory valuation concept exists in any of the 29 streams. Life/annuity statutory valuation under the Standard Valuation Law is a distinct, mandatory process — a life regulator would flag the model as P&C-only.

additions.name: Perform Asset Adequacy Analysis & Cash Flow Testing
additions.description: Follows the proposed 'Calculate Life & Annuity Statutory Reserves' step. Perform VM-30 asset adequacy analysis (multi-scenario cash flow testing of assets backing life/annuity reserves), book any additional reserves indicated, and document results in the Actuarial Opinion Memorandum supporting the life actuarial opinion.
additions.supporting: Appointed Actuary, Capital Model Actuary, Investment Analyst
additions.inputs: Statutory reserves, asset portfolio and reinvestment data, interest-rate scenarios, liability cash flow projections
additions.outputs: Cash flow testing results, additional reserves (if indicated), Actuarial Opinion Memorandum (VM-30)
additions.deliverable: Asset adequacy analysis / Actuarial Opinion Memorandum
additions.rationale: VM-30 requires life actuarial opinions to be based on asset adequacy analysis (typically cash flow testing) per ASOP 22. Verified: no step in any stream performs asset adequacy or cash-flow testing — Investment's F-12-03 ALM step monitors duration/liquidity gaps but is not statutory reserve adequacy testing. Mandatory for the Life & Retirement book.

additions.l4: Capital adequacy, stress and catastrophe modeling
additions.name: Produce ORSA Capital Assessment Inputs
additions.description: Translate capital model output into the prospective solvency assessment required for the annual ORSA: multi-year capital projections under base and stress scenarios, group capital view, and Section 2/3 evidence handed to ERM for the ORSA Summary Report filed with the lead-state commissioner.
additions.supporting: Enterprise Risk Manager, Chief Actuary, Chief Risk Officer
additions.inputs: Capital model output, stress scenarios, business plan projections, risk appetite framework
additions.outputs: Prospective solvency assessment, ORSA capital sections, stress narratives for ORSA Summary Report
additions.rationale: NAIC Model #505 (an accreditation standard enacted in 53 jurisdictions) requires insurers/groups of Meridian's scale (>$500M individual / >$1B group premium) to conduct an annual ORSA and file a confidential ORSA Summary Report with the lead-state commissioner. Verified: ORSA/own-risk concepts appear nowhere in the 29 streams — only the word 'solvency' appears, in Finance capital management (F-11-04) and Investment ALM (F-12-03), neither of which is an ORSA. The Risk stream would logically assemble the overall ORSA Summary Report, but the prospective group capital assessment it depends on is produced by this capital-modeling L4, so the step belongs in this flow (the missing Risk-side ORSA assembly is a gap for that stream's owner).

additions.name: Coordinate Assurance Coverage with External Audit
additions.description: Map the draft audit plan against external audit, Model Audit Rule / ICFR testing and other assurance providers (compliance testing, SOC reports); agree reliance, eliminate duplicate coverage and document the combined assurance map before the plan is finalized.
additions.supporting: Controller, Statutory Reporting Manager
additions.inputs: Draft audit plan, external audit scope, MAR/ICFR control testing plan, compliance monitoring plan, SOC reports
additions.outputs: Combined assurance / reliance map, deduplicated coverage plan, coordination calendar
additions.rationale: IIA Standard 2050 (Standard 9.5 in the 2024 Global Internal Audit Standards) requires the CAE to coordinate with and consider reliance on other assurance providers; under the NAIC Model Audit Rule (#205) an insurer of Meridian's size must have both an external CPA audit and management ICFR reporting, which internal audit must coordinate with. Verified: no external-audit, MAR/ICFR, or assurance-reliance step exists anywhere in the 29 streams (the Risk stream's RC-20-02 compliance-testing lifecycle does not cover it).

additions.name: Obtain Audit Committee Approval of Audit Plan
additions.description: Present the risk-based audit plan, resource budget and impact of any limitations to the Audit Committee for formal approval before the plan is published, and communicate significant interim plan changes for re-approval, per IIA Standard 2020 and the audit committee duties in the NAIC Model Audit Rule. Follows the proposed 'Coordinate Assurance Coverage with External Audit' step and precedes plan publication (S05).
additions.supporting: Board Governance Lead
additions.inputs: Final draft audit plan, resource and budget requirements, audit universe priorities, combined assurance map
additions.outputs: Committee-approved audit plan, approval minutes, communicated plan changes
additions.rationale: IIA Standard 2020 (Standard 9.4 in the 2024 Global Standards) makes board/audit-committee approval of the plan and budget mandatory, and the NAIC Model Audit Rule assigns insurers' audit committees explicit oversight duties. Verified: RC-19-01 has no governance approval step and no committee-approval step exists anywhere in the outline — RC-19-03 produces 'committee materials' but only for reporting findings/ratings, not plan approval. Anchor amended from after-S05 to after-S04 so approval precedes plan publication (the endorsed renaming makes S05 'Publish Audit Plan & Schedule'); it should be sequenced after the external-audit coordination step also anchored at S04.

additions.name: Execute Internal & External Quality Assessments
additions.description: Operate the QAIP: ongoing engagement-level quality monitoring and periodic self-assessments, commission an independent external assessment at least every five years, report results and conformance with IIA Standards to senior management and the Audit Committee, and track improvement actions.
additions.supporting: Audit Associate, Board Governance Lead
additions.inputs: QAIP framework, engagement workpapers, performance metrics, prior assessment results, IIA Standards
additions.outputs: Ongoing monitoring results, periodic self-assessments, external quality assessment report, improvement action plan, conformance statement
additions.rationale: IIA Standards 1300–1312 (QAIP provisions carried into the 2024 Global Internal Audit Standards, effective January 2025) mandate a quality assurance and improvement program covering all of internal audit, including an external assessment at least every five years; without it the function cannot state conformance with IIA Standards. Verified: no quality-assessment activity for the audit function exists anywhere in the 29 streams (AIOps' TD-28-10 model assurance is unrelated).

additions.name: Build & Maintain Service Topology and Dependency Maps
additions.description: Run automated discovery and CMDB reconciliation to build and continuously refresh service topology and dependency maps (apps, infrastructure, integrations, business services), publishing the topology model consumed by event correlation, alert enrichment and impact analysis.
additions.supporting: SRE, Infrastructure / Network Engineer, Enterprise Architect
additions.inputs: Automated discovery scans, CMDB configuration items, deployment metadata, integration inventories, business service definitions
additions.outputs: Reconciled service topology model, dependency maps, business-service impact mappings, topology feed to event correlation
additions.rationale: TD-28-03-S01 (event correlation) consumes 'topology' as an input — and Cybersecurity's TR-25-04-S01 (BCP/DR validation) consumes 'dependency maps' — yet verified no step in any of the 29 streams produces or maintains topology/CMDB/service maps (searched topology, CMDB, dependency map, service map, configuration item). Gartner and AIOps vendors consistently identify accurate, discovery-fed topology/CMDB context as a non-negotiable prerequisite for AIOps correlation, noise reduction and impact analysis — two dangling inputs a practitioner would flag.

additions.name: Process Premium Refunds & Screen Disbursements
additions.description: Calculate and disburse return premium and overpayment refunds (cancellations, endorsements, true overpayments), screening every refund payee against OFAC/sanctions lists before funds leave the company and blocking/escalating any match.
additions.supporting: Cash Application Specialist, Financial Crime AML Officer, Billing Analyst
additions.inputs: Cleared suspense items flagged for refund, return-premium calculations from policy admin, payee details, sanctions list data
additions.outputs: Issued refund payments, refund register, sanctions screening results, blocked-payment escalations
additions.deliverable: Refund disbursement register with sanctions screening evidence
additions.rationale: Verified: CI-01-02-S05 ('Resolve & Clear Suspense') only mentions 'process refunds' in its description with no disbursement step or refund output anywhere, and Policy Admin CI-04-02-S03 ('Calculate Premium Impact') produces the premium/return-premium calculation with no downstream disbursement consumer. OFAC's amended 2024 insurance FAQs (FAQ 65) direct insurers to screen at any point of sanctions exposure including outbound payments, on a strict-liability basis. Searched all 29 streams: zero hits for refund disbursement, OFAC, sanctions, or watchlist screening anywhere in the model.

additions.name: Monitor Stale Items & Escheat Unclaimed Funds
additions.description: Track uncashed refund/disbursement checks and aged unapplied cash, perform statutory due-diligence owner outreach, and report and remit dormant funds to states as unclaimed property (NAUPA-compliant filings).
additions.supporting: Treasury Analyst, Compliance Analyst, Receivables Manager
additions.inputs: Outstanding check register, aged unapplied cash, state dormancy rules, last-known owner addresses
additions.outputs: Due-diligence letters, escheatment file, state remittances, cleared stale items
additions.deliverable: Annual NAUPA unclaimed property report and remittance package
additions.rationale: Verified: state unclaimed property laws (typically 3-5 year dormancy) require insurers to perform due-diligence outreach and escheat uncashed premium refunds and stale checks in NAUPA II format, with multi-year audit lookbacks; regulators and auditors routinely flag its absence. Searched all 29 streams under escheat/unclaimed/stale/dormant: the concept appears nowhere in the model, including Finance, Treasury & Capital Management (F-11-03 treasury L4 is a generic template with no escheatment content).

additions.name: Issue Statutory Non-Pay Cancellation Notice
additions.description: When dunning and payment arrangements fail, issue the state-compliant notice of cancellation for non-payment (mandated notice periods, overdue amount, cure instructions), set the policy to pending-cancel, and hand off to Policy Administration for cancellation processing and earned-premium calculation.
additions.supporting: Billing Collections Manager, Policy Administrator, Compliance Analyst
additions.inputs: Defaulted payment arrangements, delinquent account list, state cancellation notice rules, policy data
additions.outputs: Statutory cancellation notices issued, pending-cancel status, cancellation handoff to policy admin, earned-premium billing trigger
additions.deliverable: Notice of cancellation for non-payment (proof-of-mailing retained)
additions.rationale: Verified: for in-force policies the industry-standard collections lever is statutory non-pay cancellation, not external collections; states mandate specific notice periods (10-15 days for non-payment, e.g. NY 15 days for private passenger auto, FL 627.4133 10 days) and content, and DOIs sanction defective notices. The current flow jumps from payment arrangements (S05) straight to write-off/external escalation (S06). Cancellation processing exists in Policy Admin CI-04-02 (generic 'Receive Change Request' / 'Generate Change Documentation'), but the billing-side statutory notice and trigger — what regulators examine — exists nowhere; this step explicitly hands off to CI-04-02.

additions.name: Approve & Process Write-Offs
additions.description: Review write-off recommendations against authority limits, obtain documented approval, post bad-debt write-off and allowance adjustments to the receivable subledger and GL, and refer residual earned-premium balances to external collection agencies.
additions.supporting: Billing Collections Manager, Controller, AR Reconciliation Analyst
additions.inputs: Write-off recommendations, collection history, write-off authority matrix, account balances
additions.outputs: Approved write-offs, posted bad-debt journal entries, external agency referrals, allowance updates
additions.deliverable: Approved write-off journal entries with authorization evidence
additions.rationale: Verified: CI-01-03-S06 outputs 'write-off recommendations' that no step in any stream consumes — a confirmed dangling handoff. Documented write-off approval under an authority matrix is a standard SOX/financial-reporting control activity over receivables (COSO control activities); auditors flag receivables processes that recommend but never authorize/post write-offs. Searched all 29 streams: no write-off approval or bad-debt processing step exists anywhere.
sources: AICPA audit guidance on allowance for doubtful accounts / receivables controls

additions.name: Mobilize Sponsorship & Change Network
additions.description: Build the sponsor roadmap and coalition, secure visible executive sponsorship commitments, recruit and brief a change-champion network in impacted business areas, and prepare the resistance management plan before communications and training begin.
additions.supporting: Communications Specialist, Program Mgmt Office, HR Business Partner
additions.inputs: Stakeholder map, impact assessment, change approach, adoption risks
additions.outputs: Sponsor roadmap, signed sponsorship commitments, change champion roster, resistance management plan
additions.rationale: Verified: Prosci's research consistently ranks active, visible sponsorship as the #1 change success factor, and its Phase 1 (Prepare Approach) requires a sponsorship model and resistance plan before the manage-change phase; ADKAR's Desire element is driven by sponsors and champions. Searched all 29 streams for sponsor/champion/coalition/resistance: zero hits — the model goes straight from impact analysis (CS-07-01, ending at S05 Finalize & Handoff) to comms/training prep (CS-07-02) with no sponsorship or change-network activity anywhere, so it correctly slots after CS-07-01-S05.

additions.name: Validate Death Certificate & Verify Beneficiary
additions.description: For life and annuity death claims: obtain and validate the certified death certificate, verify beneficiary designation and claimant identity, flag policies within the two-year contestability period for underwriting review, and start the statutory death-benefit interest accrual clock.
additions.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Compliance Analyst, Annuity Service Specialist
additions.inputs: Certified death certificate, claimant statement and ID, beneficiary designation on file, policy issue date
additions.outputs: Verified beneficiary entitlement, contestability flag, proof-of-loss receipt date, interest accrual start
additions.rationale: Verified: Meridian is a combined P&C + Life & Retirement insurer, yet this is the only claims-intake stream and it is entirely P&C-shaped — searched all 29 streams for death/beneficiary/contestability/life claim and found zero hits, despite Life Claims Examiner and Life Policy Service Representative existing in the role inventory. Death-claim adjudication requires a certified death certificate, beneficiary/identity verification, two-year contestability review, and statutory interest on delayed payment from proof of loss; the NAIC Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Model Act also requires DMF-driven beneficiary location. Slots after CI-02-01-S02 (Verify Policy Coverage) where claim-type-specific validation begins.

additions.name: Apply Catastrophe Event Coding & Surge Routing
additions.description: Match incoming losses to declared catastrophe events (PCS serial numbers / internal CAT codes), tag claims for CAT reporting and reinsurance recovery aggregation, and route eligible claims to fast-track handling or surge/CAT adjuster teams under the activated CAT response plan.
additions.supporting: Claims Director / Manager, Exposure Mgmt Manager, Claims Intake Rep
additions.inputs: Declared CAT event list (PCS serial numbers), loss date/location, claim severity view, CAT staffing plan
additions.outputs: CAT-coded claims, fast-track designations, surge team assignments, CAT claim inventory for reinsurance and regulators
additions.rationale: Verified: Verisk PCS assigns catastrophe serial numbers within 24-48 hours of qualifying events and carriers code claims to them at FNOL for surge routing, DOI data calls, and per-event reinsurance recovery aggregation — the Reinsurance and Claims Recoveries streams depend on event-coded claims. CAT events multiply claim volume 10-20x overnight. Searched all 29 streams: 'catastrophe' appears only in actuarial cat *modeling* inputs (RF-21-03-S01); no operational CAT claims response exists anywhere. Slots after severity assessment (S04) so CAT routing drives handler assignment (S05).

additions.name: Resolve Medicare & Lien Obligations (Section 111 / MSP)
additions.description: For bodily-injury, no-fault and similar claims: query Medicare entitlement of claimants, report ORM/TPOC to CMS under Section 111 as the Responsible Reporting Entity, resolve Medicare conditional payments and other statutory liens (Medicaid, medical, child support), and reflect lien holdbacks in settlement terms before authority and payment.
additions.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Litigation Counsel, Medical Claims Reviewer
additions.inputs: Claimant identity (SSN/HICN), negotiated settlement terms, CMS query results, conditional payment letters, lien notices
additions.outputs: Section 111 ORM/TPOC reports filed, conditional payment resolution, lien releases, lien-adjusted settlement terms
additions.deliverable: Section 111 report and conditional-payment resolution record
additions.rationale: Verified: Section 111 of the MMSEA makes liability/no-fault/WC insurers Responsible Reporting Entities, with tiered civil money penalties up to $1,000 per day per beneficiary for late TPOC/ORM reporting (CMS final rule), and Medicare asserts conditional-payment recovery against settlements. The current flow goes Negotiate Settlement (S02) → Authority (S03) → Payment (S04) with no Medicare verification or lien resolution; settling and paying without it is a material compliance failure every US casualty practitioner would flag. Searched all 29 streams for Medicare/Section 111/lien/conditional payment: zero hits anywhere in the model.

additions.name: Screen Claim Payees Against Sanctions Lists
additions.description: Screen all claim payees (claimants, providers, attorneys, vendors, lienholders) against OFAC SDN and other watchlists immediately before payment release; on a potential match, hold payment, perform due diligence, and block funds to an interest-bearing account with OFAC reporting if confirmed.
additions.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Financial Crime AML Officer, Claims Adjuster
additions.inputs: Approved settlement terms, payee identities and W-9 data, current OFAC/sanctions list data
additions.outputs: Screening results, cleared payment release, blocked-funds actions and OFAC reports for matches
additions.deliverable: Payee sanctions screening result with disposition evidence
additions.rationale: Verified: OFAC's amended 2024 insurance FAQs (FAQ 65) state insurers should screen at claim submission and claim payment, with civil penalties on strict liability; a claim under a blocked portion of a policy cannot be paid without OFAC authorization — funds must be blocked, not paid. The current flow goes straight from settlement authority (S03) to payment issuance (S04) with no screening. Searched all 29 streams for OFAC/sanctions/watchlist/AML: no screening step exists anywhere in the model, so this in-line payment control cannot be claimed as owned elsewhere (the companion billing-side refund screening addition covers the separate premium-refund disbursement flow).

additions.name: Manage Salvage Disposition & Title Transfer
additions.description: Take possession of salvageable property paid under the claim, obtain/transfer title, engage the salvage vendor or auction channel, document condition and market value, and post sale proceeds back to the claim as a recovery.
additions.supporting: Subrogation Specialist, Vendor Coordinator
additions.inputs: Salvage/subrogation opportunities (from CI-02-04-S05), salvage asset details and condition, title/ownership documents, salvage vendor agreements
additions.outputs: Title transfer record, salvage sale proceeds, vendor settlement, salvage recovery posted to claim
additions.deliverable: Salvage disposition record and sale-proceeds posting
additions.rationale: Salvage is one of the two standard recovery levers (with subrogation) and is named as an upstream output (CI-02-04-S05 'Salvage/subrogation opportunities') and as an input to CI-26-01, yet no step in any of the 29 streams actually executes salvage sale/title transfer. The 'Salvage Coordinator' role appears only as supporting on the identification step CI-02-04-S05 and leads no step anywhere — the disposition work it exists for has no home. A recoveries practitioner would flag a recovery-collection L4 that collects subrogation dollars but never disposes of salvage.

additions.name: Allocate Recovery Proceeds & Reimburse Insured Deductible
additions.description: Allocate collected recovery funds between insurer and insured: reimburse the insured's deductible first (pro-rata where comparative fault or partial recovery applies), deduct only permitted pro-rata allocated loss adjustment expense, and post the net recovery to the claim financials.
additions.supporting: Claims Coordinator, Payment Processing Clerk
additions.inputs: Collected recovery funds, insured deductible amount, comparative fault percentage, allocated loss adjustment expense, state allocation rules
additions.outputs: Pro-rata allocation worksheet, deductible reimbursement payment to insured, net recovery posting, insured notification
additions.deliverable: Deductible reimbursement payment and recovery allocation worksheet
additions.rationale: The word 'deductible' appears nowhere in the entire 29-stream model. CA 10 CCR 2695.7(q) and WAC 284-30-393 require insurers to include the insured's deductible in every subrogation demand and to share recoveries with the insured on a proportionate basis, insured first; most states have equivalent rules. Failing to evidence deductible reimbursement is a classic market-conduct exam finding against subrogation operations, so the collection/closeout L4 must show it explicitly.

additions.l4: Formal complaint handling and regulatory response
additions.name: Acknowledge Complaint & Record in Complaint Register
additions.description: Send the complainant a written acknowledgment within the applicable state timeframe (e.g., 15 calendar days in CA; 21 days for DOI inquiries), enter the complaint in the statutory complaint register with NAIC function/reason/disposition coding, and start the response-deadline diary.
additions.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager
additions.inputs: Captured complaint details (from OC-14-03-S01), receipt date and channel, state acknowledgment/response deadlines, NAIC complaint coding taxonomy
additions.outputs: Acknowledgment letter sent within regulatory timeframe, complaint register entry with NAIC coding, response deadline diary
additions.deliverable: Complaint register entry and acknowledgment letter
additions.rationale: NAIC Unfair Trade Practices Act (Model #880) makes failure to maintain a complete complaint record an unfair trade practice, and Model Regulation #884 prescribes the complaint log/register insurers must keep; states add acknowledgment clocks (e.g., CA 2695.5 15-day claimant response, 21-day DOI response). The existing generic OC-14-03 steps never name the register or the acknowledgment deadline — the first artifacts a market-conduct examiner samples. Verified against all 29 streams: complaint handling exists in OC-14-03, CI-04-04 and CS-08-04, but no step anywhere mentions the register or a complaint acknowledgment (the only acknowledgment steps in the model are claim and submission acknowledgments).

additions.name: Scan & Identify Vulnerabilities
additions.description: Run automated vulnerability scans across information systems (and manual review of systems not covered by scans) at a risk-assessment-driven frequency and promptly after material system changes; validate and risk-rank findings into the vulnerability register.
additions.leads: Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead
additions.supporting: Security Analyst, Infrastructure / Network Engineer
additions.inputs: Asset inventory, automated scan results, threat intelligence, material system change notices, risk assessment
additions.outputs: Validated vulnerability findings, risk-ranked vulnerability register
additions.rationale: Verified across all 29 streams: zero occurrences of vulnerability scanning, security patching, or penetration testing anywhere in the model (the only 'vulnerab*' hit is 'vulnerable customer flags'). 23 NYCRR 500.05 explicitly requires automated vulnerability scans (with manual review of uncovered systems) and prompt scanning after material changes; NAIC Model #668 requires at-least-annual assessment of safeguard effectiveness. For a NY-licensed combined P&C/Life insurer this is a hard regulatory requirement with no home in the current model.

additions.name: Prioritize & Remediate Vulnerabilities
additions.description: Prioritize findings by exploitability and asset criticality, drive patching/configuration remediation through platform and application teams within severity-based SLAs, and route documented risk acceptances for items that cannot be remediated on time.
additions.leads: Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead
additions.supporting: Platform Engineering Lead, DevOps / Platform Automation Engineer, Application Security Lead
additions.inputs: Risk-ranked vulnerability register, patch and release schedules, severity-based remediation SLAs
additions.outputs: Deployed patches/configuration fixes, documented risk-acceptance exceptions, SLA compliance reporting
additions.deliverable: Remediation plan and patch deployment records
additions.rationale: Timely remediation and documented risk acceptance are the control regulators test after scanning; 23 NYCRR 500 (Second Amendment) tightened expectations for timely remediation of material vulnerabilities. Without this step the new L4 would identify issues with no closure loop — an immediate examiner finding.

additions.name: Conduct Annual Penetration Test & Validate Remediation
additions.description: Commission at-least-annual penetration testing from inside and outside the information system boundary by a qualified internal or external party, retest remediated findings, and report results and residual risk to the CISO and governance forums.
additions.supporting: Vulnerability Management Lead / Security Engineering Lead, Chief Info Security Officer
additions.inputs: Pen-test scope and rules of engagement, prior-year findings, remediation evidence, risk assessment
additions.outputs: Penetration test report, retest/validation evidence, residual-risk reporting to CISO and board
additions.rationale: 23 NYCRR 500.05 requires annual penetration testing from both inside and outside the system boundary by a qualified party — a distinct obligation from scanning that no step in any stream currently satisfies. Pen-test reports are standing evidence requests in NYDFS exams and cyber-insurance placements.

additions.l4: Monitoring, incident response and cyber containment
additions.name: Determine Notification Obligations & Escalate to Compliance
additions.description: Assess whether the investigated incident is a reportable cybersecurity event (nonpublic information of 250+ consumers, material harm likelihood, or material operations impact), start the 72-hour commissioner-notification clock, and hand off to Risk & Compliance (RC-20-03) and Privacy for regulator and consumer notifications.
additions.supporting: Privacy Officer, Regulatory Affairs Manager, Privacy Counsel
additions.inputs: Investigation findings (from TR-25-03-S03), affected NPI record counts, state adoptions of NAIC Model #668, NY DFS 500.17 criteria, breach-notification statutes
additions.outputs: Reportable-event determination record, 72-hour commissioner notification handoff to RC-20-03, consumer/partner notification plan
additions.deliverable: Cybersecurity event determination and notification record
additions.rationale: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law #668 Section 6 and NY DFS 23 NYCRR 500.17 require notifying the commissioner within 72 hours of determining a cybersecurity event occurred. Regulator engagement exists elsewhere (RC-20-03 'Issue response and regulator engagement' lists breaches among its inputs and notifications among its outputs), but the incident-response runbook itself (TR-25-03) has no step that makes the determination and starts the clock — the flow runs Investigate, Contain & Eradicate, Recover with no notification gate. The determination must live inside the IR flow because the 72-hour clock starts there; this step explicitly hands off to the existing RC-20-03 process rather than duplicating it.

additions.l4: Data demand intake and model design
additions.name: Source & License External Data
additions.description: Identify and acquire third-party/external data needed by the data product (e.g. credit-based insurance scores, MIB, MVR, prescription histories, telematics), perform data-vendor due diligence, verify permissible use under FCRA/consent conditions, execute the data license, and register the source with its usage restrictions before build begins.
additions.supporting: Vendor Manager, Privacy Counsel, Data Steward
additions.inputs: Develop Approach results, external data requirements, candidate vendor offerings, FCRA/consent and permissible-use constraints
additions.outputs: Executed data license, third-party data due-diligence record, registered external source with usage restrictions
additions.rationale: Insurers depend heavily on third-party data, and the NAIC Model Bulletin on the Use of AI Systems (adopted by roughly half of states) makes insurers responsible for due diligence on third-party data and models, with audit/transparency rights; FCRA governs consumer-report data used in underwriting/rating. Verified absent: zero hits anywhere in the 29-stream outline for external data, third-party data, data license, FCRA, credit bureau, MIB, MVR or telematics; OC-13 vendor due diligence (OC-13-01-S02) covers generic vendor capability/risk, not data permissible-use. A regulator applying the AI bulletin would flag intake-to-build with no third-party-data gate. Placement after Develop Approach and before Build & Configure is correct since licensed sources must be secured before build.
sources: FCRA (15 U.S.C. §1681) adverse-action and permissible-purpose requirements

additions.l4: Data standards, stewardship and quality control
additions.name: Maintain Data Catalog & Lineage
additions.description: Populate and maintain the business glossary, enterprise data catalog and end-to-end lineage maps for governed data domains, so that certified datasets, reports and models can be traced back to authoritative sources; keep catalog entries current as sources and pipelines change.
additions.supporting: Data Modeler, Data Engineer, Data Architect
additions.inputs: Data standards, ownership matrix, source-system metadata, pipeline definitions
additions.outputs: Business glossary, data catalog entries, end-to-end lineage maps
additions.rationale: Metadata management is a core DAMA-DMBOK knowledge area, and traceability of data feeding pricing/underwriting/AI models is expected under the NAIC AI Model Bulletin (documentation and traceability of AI system inputs) and under financial-reporting data controls (MAR). Verified absent: the only catalog/lineage/metadata hits in the entire outline are a feature-store lineage output in MLOps (TD-29) and unrelated runbook/model-registry mentions — a data-management stream without metadata/lineage management would be flagged by any practitioner. Sequenced after Assign Data Ownership so stewards own their catalog domains, before Monitor Data Quality which depends on cataloged definitions.

additions.name: Screen Partner for Sanctions & Financial Crime
additions.description: Screen the coverholder/MGA legal entity, principals and beneficial owners against OFAC SDN and international sanctions lists, PEP/adverse-media sources, and assess the partner's own AML/sanctions controls; assign a financial-crime risk rating, escalate hits, and set the re-screening cadence for the relationship.
additions.supporting: Financial Crime AML Officer, Delegated Authority Manager
additions.inputs: Partner legal-entity details, principals and beneficial owners, OFAC SDN and international sanctions lists, adverse media, partner financial-crime control documentation
additions.outputs: Sanctions/watchlist screening results, financial-crime risk rating, escalation decisions, re-screening schedule
additions.rationale: Lloyd's requires managing agents and coverholders to operate proportionate sanctions due-diligence/screening programmes and financial-crime (AML, bribery) controls as a condition of delegated authority (web-verified against current Lloyd's delegated-authority guidance), and OFAC liability for transacting with listed parties is strict. Verified absent: sanctions/OFAC/watchlist/AML/financial-crime appear nowhere in any of the 29 streams; CI-03-01 verifies licenses, financials and performance but never screens the partner or its owners. The inventory even contains a Financial Crime AML Officer role that is otherwise orphaned. Sequenced after license verification, before deeper financial assessment (no point assessing a prohibited party).

additions.l4: Delegated authority terms and control design
additions.name: Define Claims Handling Authority & TPA Arrangements
additions.description: Decide whether and how far claims-handling authority is delegated to the coverholder or a third-party administrator (TPA/DCA): assess claims capability against suitability criteria, set per-claim settlement and reserve thresholds, define escalation triggers for claims outside authority, and specify claims SLAs and reporting for incorporation into the agreement.
additions.supporting: Delegated Authority Manager, Compliance Officer
additions.inputs: Claims philosophy, partner/TPA claims capability assessment, binding authority limits, DCA/TPA suitability criteria and SLA templates
additions.outputs: Claims authority schedule, TPA/DCA appointment terms, settlement and reserve thresholds, claims escalation rules
additions.rationale: Industry practice (Lloyd's Intermediaries Byelaw, LMA9008/LMA9188 TPA & delegated-claims agreements) treats claims-handling delegation as a distinct decision from underwriting authority, with its own suitability criteria, settlement thresholds and SLAs. Verified absent: 'TPA', 'third-party administrator', 'claims authority' and 'delegated claims' have zero hits across the 29-stream outline; CI-03-02 designs only underwriting appetite, binding limits and bordereaux, leaving the agreement executed in CI-03-02-S06 silent on who can determine and pay claims — a gap a Lloyd's or DOI delegated-authority reviewer would flag immediately. Placed after Establish Authority Limits so claims authority is set alongside underwriting limits, before Design Control Framework and agreement drafting.

additions.name: Reconcile Premium Settlements to Bordereaux
additions.description: Match cash remittances received from the coverholder/MGA against premium reported on validated bordereaux, confirm settlement within agreed terms of trade, verify fiduciary/trust handling of premium funds, age and chase unsettled balances, and escalate persistent late settlement as an authority breach.
additions.supporting: Cash Application Specialist, Delegated Authority Manager
additions.inputs: Validated premium bordereaux, settlement remittances, agreement payment terms (terms of trade), premium trust/fiduciary account requirements
additions.outputs: Bordereaux-to-cash settlement reconciliation, aged unsettled-balance report, late-settlement escalations
additions.rationale: Coverholders collect premium on the carrier's behalf and must remit it within terms of trade with fiduciary protection — Lloyd's premium-and-claims-handling standards require managing agents to monitor that reported premium is actually settled. Verified: CI-03-03 validates bordereaux data quality and KPIs but never reconciles money; corporate daily cash recon (CI-01-02-S06 'Reconcile Daily Cash') and reinsurance cession settlement (CI-05-03-S06 'Process Cash Settlements') both exist elsewhere as claimed but neither covers delegated-partner premium settlement, so unremitted premium would go undetected. Placed after Validate Bordereaux Data since reconciliation requires validated premium figures, before KPI analysis.

additions.name: Screen Producer Background & Watchlists
additions.description: Run criminal background checks and OFAC/watchlist screening on the producer/agency and its principals, check NIPR/state records for license status and regulatory actions, identify 18 U.S.C. §1033 disqualifying convictions (dishonesty/breach-of-trust felonies) and require written regulator consent (1033 waiver) where applicable, and clear or escalate before setup proceeds.
additions.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Producer Compliance Manager
additions.inputs: Producer/agency application, SSN/TIN, criminal background results, OFAC SDN list, NIPR license and regulatory-action data
additions.outputs: Background and sanctions clearance, 1033 consent flags and waiver requests, disqualification escalations
additions.rationale: 18 U.S.C. §1033 makes it unlawful for an insurer to willfully permit a person with a dishonesty/breach-of-trust felony to engage in the business of insurance without regulator written consent (civil penalties up to $50,000 per occurrence), and carriers routinely OFAC-screen producers and agency principals at appointment and renewal. Verified absent: 'background check', '1033', OFAC and watchlist screening have zero hits anywhere in the 29-stream outline; PG-16-02 collects licensing status and PG-16-03-S02 contracts producers with no compliance gate between. Placed after Collect Inputs and before Configure & Set Up so no system access is provisioned to an unscreened producer.

additions.name: File State Producer Appointments
additions.description: File the carrier appointment for each producer with the relevant state insurance departments (via NIPR or state portals) within the statutory window, pay appointment fees, record confirmations in the appointment register, and schedule renewal-fee maintenance so the producer is legally authorized to sell for Meridian before activation.
additions.supporting: Producer Licensing Specialist, Compliance Analyst
additions.inputs: Cleared and QC'd producer record, state appointment forms and fee schedules, NIPR gateway access
additions.outputs: Filed state appointments, fee payment confirmations, updated appointment register, renewal schedule
additions.rationale: Web-verified: NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act (#218) §14 requires an insurer authorizing a producer to act as its agent to file a notice of appointment with the commissioner within 15 days of the agency contract or first application; producers selling without an active appointment expose the carrier to fines and market-conduct findings. Verified absent: the word 'appointment' (producer sense) appears nowhere in the 29-stream outline — onboarding goes straight from Validate & QC to Activate & Handoff with no regulatory filing, a gap any state examiner would flag. Placed after Validate & QC and before Activate & Handoff so the producer is legally appointed before activation.

additions.name: Terminate Producers & Notify Regulators
additions.description: Execute producer/partner termination decisions from governance: terminate state appointments and notify each insurance commissioner within 30 days (with supporting documentation and producer copy where termination is for cause), revoke portal/system access, settle final commissions per contract, and archive the relationship file per retention policy.
additions.supporting: Producer Compliance Manager, Broker Relationship Mgr
additions.inputs: Termination/non-renewal decisions, for-cause documentation, appointment register, commission balances
additions.outputs: Terminated appointments, DOI termination notices, producer notification letters, access revocation confirmations, final commission settlement instructions
additions.rationale: Web-verified: NAIC PLMA Model #218 requires insurers to notify the commissioner within 30 days of terminating a producer's appointment — with documentation when termination is for one of the enumerated causes — and to notify the producer. Verified in outline: PG-16-04-S05 outputs include 'renewal decisions' with no step executing them, CI-03-04-S06 terminates delegated authorities only, and 'offboarding' exists solely in the vendor stream (OC-13); no step anywhere executes producer termination, files the regulatory notice, or offboards access/commissions — the producer lifecycle currently has an entrance and no exit. Appended after the final governance step (S05) which produces the termination/renewal decisions it consumes.

additions.name: Track Benefits Realization Against Business Cases
additions.description: Compare actual financial and operational outcomes of funded initiatives against the benefits committed in their approved business cases; confirm benefit owners, quantify realization-to-date and variance, and feed the scorecard into the executive assessment step.
additions.supporting: FP&A Manager, Financial Analyst
additions.inputs: Approved business cases and benefit commitments, funding approvals and capital allocations (EM-10-03 outputs), initiative delivery status, actual financial and operational results
additions.outputs: Benefits realization scorecard, variance-to-business-case analysis, benefit-owner corrective actions
additions.rationale: Verified: EM-10-04-S01 lists 'benefits tracking' as an input, yet no step in any of the 29 streams produces benefits-realization data — business cases are created upstream (PG-18-02-S02 'Develop Business Case' in Product & Proposition Management) and consumed by EM-10-02/EM-10-03 funding decisions, but nothing ever validates realized outcomes against them (confirmed via search for 'benefit', 'realization', 'business case', 'ROI', 'value/outcome tracking' across the full outline). SAFe Lean Portfolio Management and PMI Benefits Realization Management both treat outcome/realization tracking as the core feedback loop of portfolio governance — without it the funding decisions made in EM-10-03 are never validated, a gap any portfolio-assurance review would flag.

additions.name: Reconcile Provider Invoices to Usage Data & General Ledger
additions.description: Validate monthly cloud provider invoices against billing/usage exports and allocation rules, resolve timing and credit/discount variances, and post reconciled chargeback amounts to the correct GL cost centers before chargeback statements are finalized.
additions.supporting: FinOps Lead, Controller
additions.inputs: Cloud provider invoices, billing/usage export (FOCUS-format cost data), allocation rules, GL cost-center mapping, prior-period variance log
additions.outputs: Invoice-to-usage reconciliation, GL journal postings for chargeback, variance and credit log
additions.rationale: Web-verified: the FinOps Foundation 'Invoicing & Chargeback' capability explicitly covers receiving, validating and reconciling provider invoices and tying chargeback to General Ledger codes (the GL Recharge Rate KPI exists precisely to prove booked cloud spend matches the CSP bill). T-27-02 produces showback/chargeback statements (T-27-02-S05 output) from usage data but never validates them against what Meridian is actually billed and books — cloud spend would hit the GL unreconciled, a control gap Finance and internal audit would flag. Absence confirmed: 'invoice' appears only in premium billing (CI-01-01), claims damage assessment and reinsurer billing (CI-05-04); no cloud-invoice reconciliation exists anywhere in the outline.

additions.name: Identify Dormant Property & Perform Owner Due Diligence
additions.description: Identify uncashed claim and refund checks, dormant policyholder credits, matured policies and retained asset accounts that have reached state dormancy thresholds; perform required due-diligence outreach (letters, DMF-match follow-up) to locate owners and beneficiaries before escheatment.
additions.supporting: Cash Application Specialist, Life Policy Service Representative, Compliance Analyst
additions.inputs: Aged uncashed checks register, dormant policyholder/premium credits, matured policy and retained-asset-account lists, Death Master File match results, state dormancy schedules
additions.outputs: Dormancy aging report, due-diligence letters issued, reactivated or located-owner items removed from escheat population
additions.rationale: Absence verified: no escheatment or unclaimed-property process exists anywhere in the 29-stream model (zero hits for 'escheat', 'unclaimed', 'dormant', 'uncashed', 'DMF'/'Death Master'). Every US state requires holders — and insurers are major holders via uncashed claim checks and unclaimed death benefits — to perform due diligence (NAUPA: certified-mail notice 60–120 days before reporting for items over the threshold) and remit. Life insurers face heightened obligations (DMF comparison, unclaimed-benefits acts) following multistate regulatory settlements, so the absence is a guaranteed market-conduct/audit finding for a combined P&C + Life carrier.

additions.name: Report & Remit Unclaimed Property to States
additions.description: Compile the final escheatable population after due diligence, prepare NAUPA-II-format state unclaimed property reports, remit funds to each state by its filing deadline, and retain holder records to support future owner claims and state audits.
additions.supporting: Treasury Analyst, Compliance Analyst, Statutory Reporting Analyst
additions.inputs: Final escheatable item list, due-diligence outcomes, state filing calendars and NAUPA II format requirements
additions.outputs: Filed state unclaimed property reports, remittance payments, retained holder records and audit trail
additions.rationale: Companion step to dormancy identification: the report-and-remit cycle is a hard statutory deadline in all US jurisdictions (NAUPA-standard format required by most states; life insurers typically on a May notice / December remit cycle) and state treasurers actively audit insurers. It belongs in Finance — the holder-reporting function is typically owned by the Controller/Tax organization — and exists nowhere in the current model (verified).

additions.l4: Capital actions, tax and solvency reporting
additions.name: Prepare Tax Provision & Premium Tax Filings
additions.description: Prepare the federal and state income tax provision under SSAP 101 (current and deferred, with admissibility testing), and prepare/file state premium tax, retaliatory tax and municipal tax returns with estimated payments, feeding the provision into statutory and capital reporting.
additions.supporting: Tax Director, Statutory Reporting Analyst, Controller
additions.inputs: Approved financial statements, written premium by state and line, SSAP 101 workpapers, state premium tax rates and retaliatory tax rules, estimated payment schedules
additions.outputs: SSAP 101 income tax provision and DTA admissibility analysis, state premium tax and retaliatory tax returns, estimated tax payments
additions.deliverable: Premium tax returns & SSAP 101 tax provision
additions.rationale: Verified: the L4 is literally named 'Capital actions, tax and solvency reporting' yet contains zero tax steps, and no premium-tax or income-tax process exists anywhere in the 29 streams — the only 'tax' hit outside this L4's name is CI-01-01-S02's policy-level 'tax/fee rules' surcharge application, which is not corporate tax compliance. The roles 'Tax Analyst' and 'Tax Director' exist in the role inventory but are confirmed unused by any step. Premium taxes are among the largest expense lines for US insurers, and the statutory annual statement cannot be completed without the SSAP 101 provision. Placed after step 5 so filings flow into S06 'Report to Regulators'.

additions.name: Screen Outbound Treasury Payments Against Sanctions Lists
additions.description: Screen all outbound treasury disbursements (wires, ACH, intercompany and vendor payments) and their counterparties against OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists before release; hold potential matches, escalate to financial-crime compliance for disposition, and retain a screening audit trail.
additions.supporting: Financial Crime AML Officer, Compliance Analyst
additions.inputs: Outbound payment batch, counterparty/beneficiary master data, OFAC SDN and consolidated screening lists, match-disposition and escalation procedures
additions.outputs: Screened payment release file, potential-match holds and dispositions, escalations to compliance, screening audit trail
additions.deliverable: Sanctions screening log for treasury disbursements
additions.rationale: Absence independently verified: zero hits for 'sanction', 'OFAC', 'watchlist', 'AML', 'KYC' or 'financial crime' anywhere in the 29-stream outline — despite 'Financial Crime AML Officer' existing in the role inventory. The enterprise sanctions program rightly belongs to Risk, Compliance & Regulatory Management (not this stream), but OFAC's Framework for Compliance Commitments and its insurance-industry FAQs expect a screening control embedded at each payment-execution point; an unscreened treasury disbursement flow exposes Meridian to strict-liability OFAC violations. Correctly placed as the payment-execution control between Execute & Process (S03) and Validate & Control (S04).

additions.name: Reconcile Positions & Cash with Custodian
additions.description: Reconcile the investment book of record (positions, cash, trades, corporate actions) against custodian bank statements on a daily/monthly cycle; investigate and clear breaks before valuation. Confirms that securities held under custodial agreements are separately identified as insurer-owned, as NAIC examiners require.
additions.supporting: Treasury Analyst, Senior Accountant
additions.inputs: Custodian statements, settled trade records, investment book of record, corporate action notices
additions.outputs: Reconciled positions and cash, break/exception log with resolution actions
additions.rationale: The L4 goes straight from Settle Transactions (S04) to Value Portfolio (S05) with no reconciliation control. Reconciliation steps elsewhere in the model (daily cash CI-01-02-S06, billing-to-ledger CI-01-04, GL account recs F-11-01-S03, reinsurance accounts CI-05-04-S04) are all unrelated — no step anywhere reconciles investment positions/cash to the custodian. NAIC Financial Condition Examiners Handbook guidance on custodial/safekeeping agreements makes custody controls and verification of custodian records an examination focus — valuation and Schedule D data are unreliable without this step. The Investment Operations Manager role exists in the inventory but is unused in this stream.

additions.name: Monitor Investment Guideline & Limit Compliance
additions.description: Run post-trade surveillance of the valued portfolio against the board-approved investment policy and statutory limits (asset-class caps, single-issuer concentration, admitted-asset percentages, rating floors); log breaches, escalate to the CIO/CRO and track cure actions to closure.
additions.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Portfolio Manager, Enterprise Risk Manager
additions.inputs: Valued portfolio positions, investment policy limits, state investment statutes and NAIC limit tables, issuer/counterparty exposure data
additions.outputs: Guideline compliance results, breach alerts, escalation and cure-plan actions
additions.rationale: NAIC Investments of Insurers Model Acts (#280 defined-limits / #283 defined-standards) require the insurer to establish internal controls and procedures to assure compliance with its board-approved written investment policy and statutory limits (e.g., single-issuer caps of 3% of admitted assets for life and 5% for non-life insurers; non-compliant assets become non-admitted). The stream has no compliance-monitoring step — F-12-02-S04 'Validate & Control' is a generic pre-release check inside rebalancing; the only breach-monitoring in the model is delegated-authority oversight (CI-03-03), which does not cover the investment portfolio. Verified: 'guideline'/'breach' hits in all 29 streams are underwriting, budgeting, and delegated-authority items only.

additions.name: Assess Impairments & Maintain NAIC Designations
additions.description: Quarterly (after Value Portfolio and guideline monitoring, before Report Performance): screen the portfolio for credit events and unrealized-loss positions, perform other-than-temporary-impairment analysis under SSAP 26R/43R, book write-downs to a new cost basis, and refresh NAIC SVO designations feeding Schedule D and RBC.
additions.supporting: Statutory Reporting Analyst, Senior Accountant
additions.inputs: Portfolio valuation, credit events and watchlist securities, SVO Purposes & Procedures Manual designations, SSAP impairment guidance
additions.outputs: Impairment decisions and recorded write-downs, updated NAIC designations, Schedule D-ready investment data
additions.deliverable: Impairment assessment memo & Schedule D investment data
additions.rationale: A statutory filer must run OTTI/impairment analysis and maintain SVO credit designations every quarter — Schedule D Part 1 reporting and AVR/RBC factors depend on them. Verified: 'impairment', 'SVO', 'NAIC designation', and 'Schedule D' have zero hits across all 29 streams, yet Finance's F-11-01-S06 'File Regulatory Reports' consumes this data; without the step the chain from valuation to statutory filing is broken. Regulators (and auditors) would flag this immediately at a combined P&C + Life carrier.

additions.l4: Litigation, complaints and regulatory response handling
additions.name: Issue Legal Hold & Preserve Records
additions.description: Immediately after a matter is captured: determine whether litigation is pending or reasonably anticipated, identify custodians and data sources, suspend routine deletion/auto-purge, issue legal hold notices, and track custodian acknowledgments and periodic reminders until release.
additions.supporting: Legal Operations Manager / Corporate Paralegal, Paralegal
additions.inputs: Litigation or regulatory matter notice, custodian and data-source map, records retention schedules
additions.outputs: Legal hold notices issued, custodian acknowledgments, preservation scope and release criteria
additions.rationale: FRCP 37(e) imposes a duty to preserve ESI once litigation is reasonably anticipated; failure risks spoliation sanctions, adverse-inference instructions, or default judgment. CS-08-04 currently jumps from Initiate & Capture (S01) straight to Analyze & Assess (S02) with no preservation step. Verified: 'legal hold'/'preserve' have zero hits in all 29 streams; the only discovery-related step is claims-side defense litigation (CI-02-04-S10 'Manage Discovery'), which does not cover corporate, employment, or regulatory matters handled by this L4.

additions.name: Intake & Verify Privacy Rights Request
additions.description: Receive consumer requests to access, correct, delete, or opt out of processing of personal information from any channel; verify requester identity, confirm the applicable legal basis (NAIC Model #670 access/correction/deletion rights, GLBA/Model #672 notices, state comprehensive privacy laws), scope the in-store personal data, and start the statutory response clock.
additions.supporting: Data Protection Officer, Customer Service Rep
additions.inputs: Consumer access/correction/deletion/opt-out requests, identity verification evidence, statutory response deadlines, personal-data inventory
additions.outputs: Verified and classified request, scoped data inventory, assigned due date
additions.rationale: Verified: no step in any of the 29 streams handles individual privacy-rights requests under any synonym (DSAR, data subject, access/deletion request, opt-out). TD-24-04 ('Data access, retention and privacy control') governs internal access/retention controls and CS-08-03 is advisory privacy review — neither fulfills consumer requests. NAIC Model #670 grants insurance consumers access plus correction/amendment/deletion rights (30-business-day access response) in adopting states (AZ, CA, CT, GA, IL, MA, NJ, NC, OH, OR, VA and others), and the in-flight Model #672 amendments plus state comprehensive privacy laws extend them; a Privacy Officer would flag this as a day-one operational gap.

additions.name: Fulfill Request & Respond Within Statutory Deadline
additions.description: Retrieve the requester's personal data across systems, apply exemptions (claims investigation, fraud, privileged material) with documented legal basis, execute the correction/deletion/opt-out or compile the access package, respond within the statutory deadline, and log disposition for regulator examination.
additions.supporting: Data Protection Officer, Privacy Counsel
additions.inputs: Verified DSAR case record, retrieved personal data, exemption and privilege analysis
additions.outputs: Response package or executed correction/deletion/opt-out, documented denials with legal basis, completion log
additions.rationale: Completes the new DSAR L4: verification without fulfillment/response is not a defensible process. Statutory deadlines (Model #670's 30-business-day access response; 30-45 days under state comprehensive privacy laws) and documented-denial requirements — including Model #670's claims/proceeding exemption — are what DOI market-conduct examiners test; the disposition log is the examination evidence.

additions.name: Maintain Model Inventory & Risk Tiering
additions.description: Maintain the enterprise inventory of all ML/AI models and AI systems (in development, production, and third-party), capturing owner, business use, data sources, and consumer-impact characteristics; assign and refresh risk tiers that drive the depth of validation, monitoring, and Responsible AI controls applied downstream.
additions.supporting: Data Governance, Data Science Lead
additions.inputs: Registered models and versions, business use-case metadata, third-party AI/data sources, consumer-impact and harm criteria
additions.outputs: Complete model & AI system inventory with assigned risk tiers, governance scope per tier
additions.rationale: Verified dangling dependency: TD-29-08-S01 and TD-28-10-S01 (AIOps) both consume 'Model inventory' as an input, but no step in any of the 29 streams outputs one (the only inventory output anywhere is RC-20-01-S01's 'Risk inventory'). The NAIC Model AI Bulletin (adopted Dec 2023, now adopted by over half of states) expects a written AIS Program with controls commensurate with assessed risk per AI system — which presupposes a cataloged, risk-ranked inventory of every AI system in underwriting, pricing, claims, servicing, fraud and marketing; it is the first artifact a regulator requests in an AI-focused exam.

additions.name: Retire & Decommission Superseded Models
additions.description: For superseded or underperforming models: confirm no remaining consumers via the dependency map, drain and retire serving endpoints, archive model artifacts, lineage, and decision evidence per retention requirements, and update registry status and the enterprise model inventory to 'retired'.
additions.supporting: Data Science Lead, Model Risk Manager
additions.inputs: Superseded/underperforming model list, endpoint dependency map, evidence retention requirements
additions.outputs: Retired serving endpoints, archived artifacts and lineage, updated registry and inventory status
additions.rationale: The lifecycle L4 ends at deploying the retrained model (TD-29-07-S05 'updated deployments') with no controlled retirement — deprecated models keep serving predictions and the registry/inventory drift from production reality. Verified: 'retire', 'archive', 'sunset' have zero step hits across all 29 streams and the only 'decommission' hit is FinOps cloud-resource rightsizing (T-27-05-S05), unrelated to models. Industry MLOps lifecycle references (Google Cloud MLOps practitioner guide, model-registry lifecycle guidance) treat retirement/archival with evidence retention as a required terminal stage, and SR 11-7-style model risk management treats development-validation-deployment-monitoring-retirement as one governed chain with documented decommissioning.

additions.name: Review Marketing Materials for Advertising Compliance
additions.description: Review all campaign creative, messaging and product claims against state advertising regulations (NAIC Model #570 standards for life/annuity advertising, Unfair Trade Practices rules for P&C), confirm required disclosures and prohibited terms, and file the approved materials in the advertising record retained for market conduct examination.
additions.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Marketing Coordinator
additions.inputs: Draft campaign messaging, creative assets, product disclosures, state advertising rules and prohibited-terms lists
additions.outputs: Compliance-approved materials, advertising file record, required disclosure inserts
additions.deliverable: Advertising compliance sign-off and retained ad-file record
additions.rationale: NAIC Model #570 obligates insurers to maintain a system of control over the content, form and method of dissemination of ALL advertisements and to keep an advertising file for market conduct exams; violations carry fines up to $1,000 per violation and license suspension/revocation. Verified: the only 'advertis' occurrence in all 29 streams is job advertising in Talent & Workforce Management — no advertising-compliance review exists anywhere. For a life & annuity writer this is a step regulators explicitly test in market conduct exams, and it must occur before Approve & Publish (PG-17-02-S05).

additions.name: Apply Consent & Suppression Screening
additions.description: Scrub campaign audience lists against the national Do-Not-Call registry, internal opt-out/suppression lists and consent records before any outbound call, text or email execution; verify prior express written consent for autodialed/prerecorded outreach and retain timestamped consent evidence.
additions.supporting: Privacy Officer, Compliance Analyst
additions.inputs: Audience lists, consent and preference records, national DNC registry, internal suppression and opt-out logs
additions.outputs: Scrubbed audience lists, suppression evidence, timestamped consent audit trail
additions.deliverable: Scrubbed campaign audience list with consent log
additions.rationale: TCPA exposes insurers to $500-$1,500 per call/text statutory damages (class actions routinely reach millions) and CAN-SPAM requires opt-out honoring; PG-17-03-S01 lists 'contact policies' as an input but no step actually enforces them. Verified: no DNC, TCPA or suppression concept exists anywhere in the 29-stream model ('consent' appears only as a data-privacy input in TD-24-04). This control must execute between Analyze & Assess (S02) and Execute & Process (S03).

additions.l4: Life and annuity in-force transaction servicing
additions.name: Receive & Validate In-Force Transaction Request
additions.description: Accept life/annuity in-force transaction requests (beneficiary change, ownership change/assignment, surrender, partial withdrawal, policy loan, annuitization election), verify owner identity and signing authority, confirm forms are in good order, and log the transaction in the policy administration system.
additions.supporting: Annuity Service Specialist, Retirement Operations Administrator
additions.inputs: Transaction request forms (beneficiary/ownership change, surrender, withdrawal, loan), policy record, identity and authority verification
additions.outputs: Good-order transaction request, verified owner authority, logged transaction case
additions.rationale: Meridian is a combined P&C + Life & Retirement insurer, yet the Policy Administration & Servicing stream contains only P&C-shaped issuance/endorsement flows: verified that 'beneficiary', 'surrender', 'loan', 'withdrawal' and 'annuitization' appear nowhere in any of the 29 streams. The entire life in-force transaction capability — the daily core of a life servicing operation — is absent; this and the following steps form that missing chain. The role inventory already contains Life Policy Service Representative, Annuity Service Specialist and Retirement Operations Administrator, which are otherwise unused in this stream.

additions.l4: Life and annuity in-force transaction servicing
additions.name: Review Replacement & Suitability Compliance
additions.description: For surrenders, exchanges (incl. 1035) and replacements, verify replacement notices and disclosures per NAIC Model #613, apply the best-interest/suitability review required by NAIC Model #275 for annuity transactions, document the care/disclosure/conflict/documentation obligations, and route conservation or escalation where the transaction appears unsuitable.
additions.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Life Policy Service Representative
additions.inputs: Good-order transaction request, replacement disclosure forms, suitability/best-interest documentation, existing contract surrender-charge data
additions.outputs: Replacement notices, suitability/best-interest determination, conservation or escalation cases
additions.rationale: NAIC Model #275 (2020 best-interest revision, adopted in 45+ states) applies to any recommendation to purchase, EXCHANGE or REPLACE an annuity, and Model #613 governs replacement disclosures on surrenders/exchanges — both are top DOI market-conduct exam topics. Verified: no 'suitability' or 'replacement' (other than 'replacement documents' in service fulfillment) exists anywhere in the model, despite the inventory containing an Annuity Suitability Analyst role. The carrier-side review sits naturally between transaction validation and sanctions screening/disbursement.

additions.l4: Life and annuity in-force transaction servicing
additions.name: Screen Payee Against Sanctions Watchlists
additions.description: Screen the payee, policy owner and any added/changed beneficiaries against OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists before funds release; on a true match, block the transaction and policy interest, report to OFAC within 10 business days, and route blocked funds per OFAC requirements.
additions.supporting: Financial Crime AML Officer
additions.inputs: Payee and owner identity data, beneficiary details, OFAC SDN and consolidated screening lists
additions.outputs: Screening result, cleared payee or blocked-transaction escalation and OFAC report
additions.rationale: OFAC's November 13, 2024 insurance FAQ update (revised FAQ 65) directs insurers to screen at policy amendment — explicitly including the addition of insured parties or beneficiaries — and at claim/payment, and new FAQ 1199 clarifies that even payments involving innocent third parties under a blocked party's policy require OFAC authorization. Verified: NO sanctions/OFAC/watchlist screening exists anywhere in the 29-stream model — surrender and beneficiary disbursements are a primary exposure point, so the in-line check belongs here even though Compliance owns the enterprise sanctions program.

additions.l4: Life and annuity in-force transaction servicing
additions.name: Disburse Funds & Apply Tax Withholding
additions.description: Calculate surrender/withdrawal/loan values including surrender charges and market value adjustments, apply federal/state tax withholding elections, release funds to the cleared payee, update policy values and status in the system of record, and generate the 1099-R tax reporting record.
additions.supporting: Payment Processing Clerk, Tax Analyst
additions.inputs: Cleared transaction, surrender/loan value calculation, withholding elections, payee banking details
additions.outputs: Disbursed funds, updated policy values and status, 1099-R tax reporting record
additions.deliverable: Disbursement confirmation and tax withholding record
additions.rationale: Completes the life in-force transaction chain: value calculation, IRC withholding/1099-R reporting and funds release are the steps state DOIs and the IRS hold life insurers to on every surrender, withdrawal and loan. Verified: '1099', 'withhold' and 'disburse' appear nowhere in the 29 streams — without this step the proposed L4 (and the stream) has no money-out leg, and the model has no policyholder disbursement anywhere outside claims.

additions.l4: Life and annuity in-force transaction servicing
additions.name: Perform Death Master File Matching & Unclaimed Property Escheatment
additions.description: Compare in-force and lapsed life policies, annuity contracts and retained asset accounts against SSA Death Master File updates at least semi-annually using fuzzy-match rules; initiate beneficiary location and outreach on matches; track dormant proceeds and remit unclaimed funds to states per escheatment schedules.
additions.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Life Policy Service Representative
additions.inputs: In-force and lapsed policy/contract records, SSA Death Master File updates, state unclaimed-property dormancy schedules
additions.outputs: DMF match list, beneficiary outreach cases, escheated funds remittance and state filings
additions.deliverable: DMF match and escheatment compliance report
additions.rationale: The NAIC Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Model Act (#786) and the NCOIL model require insurers to compare all in-force policies, annuity contracts and retained asset accounts against DMF updates no less than twice a year with name-variant matching, begin a thorough search within four months of learning of a death, and complete it within a year; industry-wide regulatory settlements on this topic exceeded $1B (MetLife, Prudential et al. global resolution agreements). Verified: 'escheat', 'unclaimed' and 'death master' appear nowhere in any of the 29 streams — an unmistakable gap for a Life & Retirement carrier that any DOI examiner would flag immediately.

additions.name: Develop & Certify Product Illustrations
additions.description: For illustrated life products, build the illustration system from the rating plan and non-guaranteed element scales, test the disciplined current scale per ASOP 24 (self-support and lapse-support tests), and obtain the board-appointed illustration actuary's certification before the new policy form is illustrated; file the certification with regulators.
additions.supporting: Appointed Actuary, Insurance Product Manager
additions.inputs: Rating plan, non-guaranteed element scales, disciplined current scale testing per ASOP 24
additions.outputs: Compliant illustration system, illustration actuary certification filed with the board and regulators
additions.rationale: NAIC Model #582 requires the insurer to notify the commissioner whether each policy form is marketed with an illustration and requires a board-appointed illustration actuary to certify the disciplined current scale (self-support/lapse-support tested per ASOP 24) with annual recertification — a hard launch gate for UL, IUL, whole life and annuity products. Verified: 'illustration' appears nowhere in the 29-stream model, yet Meridian writes Life & Retirement business. It belongs between rating methodology (PG-18-02-S04) and forms/filing drafting (S05).

additions.name: Develop Underwriting Guidelines & Appetite Rules
additions.description: Translate the coverage design and target risk profile into underwriting guidelines: eligibility criteria, risk classification, referral thresholds, declination rules and authority levels, aligned with reinsurance treaty constraints, so the product can be consistently underwritten at launch.
additions.supporting: Insurance Product Manager, Senior Underwriter
additions.inputs: Coverage design, target risk profile and appetite, reinsurance treaty constraints
additions.outputs: Underwriting guidelines, eligibility and referral rules, authority matrix updates
additions.deliverable: Underwriting guideline manual for the new product
additions.rationale: PG-18-04-S04 explicitly REVISES 'forms, rules, and underwriting guidelines' and Submission-to-Bind consumes 'appetite guidelines' as inputs (CI-01 screening steps), but no step anywhere in this stream creates the initial guidelines — a dangling reference. The only guideline-creation step in the model (CI-03-02-S01 'Define Underwriting Appetite') is scoped to delegated-authority partner agreements, not the carrier's own products, so the gap here is real. Standard product-development practice (ACORD capability framework, carrier launch checklists) places UW rule definition between coverage design and rating/filing.

additions.name: Assess Reinsurer Security & Set Counterparty Limits
additions.description: Before marketing the treaty, evaluate each prospective reinsurer's financial strength ratings, credit-for-reinsurance status (authorized/certified/reciprocal-jurisdiction) and existing aggregate exposure; maintain the approved security list and set per-counterparty limits and collateral conditions used in placement.
additions.supporting: Head of Reinsurance, Enterprise Risk Manager, Treasury Manager
additions.inputs: AM Best/S&P ratings, reinsurer financial statements, credit-for-reinsurance status, current recoverable balances by counterparty, risk appetite
additions.outputs: Approved reinsurer security list, counterparty exposure limits, collateral requirements feeding placement
additions.rationale: Verified: CI-05-02 goes straight from Develop Treaty Structure (S02) to Market to Reinsurers (S03) with no counterparty credit/security gate, and counterparty, security list, collateral, and rating-agency review have zero hits across all 29 streams. Regulators and rating agencies expect a reinsurance security committee process; uncollectible recoverables from weak counterparties drive Schedule F penalties under NAIC credit-for-reinsurance rules (the model's only Schedule F touchpoint, CI-05-04-S05, presumes this control exists upstream).

additions.name: Notify Reinsurers of Large Losses & Cat Events
additions.description: Identify claims breaching treaty notification thresholds or arising from coded catastrophe events and issue prompt written loss advices to reinsurers/brokers per each contract's notice-of-loss clause, tracking subsequent material developments to preserve recovery rights before cessions are processed.
additions.supporting: Claims Director / Manager, Reinsurance Analyst
additions.inputs: Large-loss reports above treaty notice thresholds, cat event coding, treaty notice-of-loss clauses, claim reserve changes
additions.outputs: Timely reinsurer loss advices, cat event loss tracking, preserved recovery rights
additions.rationale: Verified: CI-05-03-S03 processes claim cessions, but contractual prompt-notice of large losses and cat events appears nowhere in the model — all 'loss notice/notification' hits are insured-facing FNOL (CI-02) or bind-time treaty coding (CI-06-04-S05), and the Claims Recoveries & Subrogation stream (CI-26) covers only subrogation. Late notice under standard notice-of-loss clauses is the leading cause of disputed or denied reinsurance recoveries; placement before Process Claim Cessions (S03) is correct since notice is a contractual precondition to recovery.

additions.l4: Claims recovery and program performance reporting
additions.name: Manage Collateral, LOCs & Trust Accounts
additions.description: Calculate collateral required from unauthorized/uncollateralized reinsurers, issue collateral calls, verify trust account balances and confirm letters of credit remain clean, irrevocable and evergreen; draw on collateral for overdue balances so statutory credit for reinsurance is preserved in Schedule F.
additions.supporting: Treasury Analyst, Reinsurance Manager
