additions.inputs: Reconciled recoverable balances by counterparty, reinsurer authorization/collateral status, LOC and trust agreements, aging over 90 days
additions.outputs: Collateral calls, verified LOC/trust positions, collateral draws on overdue balances, Schedule F penalty avoidance inputs
additions.rationale: Verified: CI-05-04 reconciles accounts (S04) and prepares Schedule F (S05) but collateral, letters of credit and trust accounts have zero hits anywhere in the 29-stream model. NAIC Models #785/#786 make collateral management the core control determining whether statutory credit for reinsurance is allowed; positioning between reconciliation (S04) and statutory reporting (S05) is correct because verified collateral positions feed Schedule F.

additions.name: Screen Parties Against Sanctions & Watchlists
additions.description: Operate risk-based OFAC/sanctions and watchlist screening of policyholders, beneficiaries, claimants, payees, producers and vendors at onboarding, renewal, amendment, claim payment and on list updates; block or reject prohibited transactions and maintain disposition evidence.
additions.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Compliance Officer
additions.inputs: Customer/claimant/payee/producer/vendor records, OFAC SDN and consolidated lists, watchlist vendor feeds, screening rules and thresholds
additions.outputs: Screening dispositions, blocked/rejected transaction log, escalated true-match alerts
additions.rationale: Verified: sanctions, OFAC and watchlist screening have zero hits across all 29 streams, and the inventory role 'Financial Crime AML Officer' leads no step anywhere in the model. OFAC's insurance-industry FAQs state insurers must screen across the policy lifecycle and block/report prohibited transactions; a regulator would flag a combined P&C + Life carrier with no sanctions screening step anywhere. Compliance owns the screening program, so the new L4 belongs in this stream under Control Monitoring (an existing L3).

additions.name: Investigate Alerts & File SARs / OFAC Reports
additions.description: Investigate escalated screening and AML monitoring alerts on covered products (permanent life, annuities), file Suspicious Activity Reports with FinCEN and blocked-property reports with OFAC within required deadlines, maintain confidentiality and 5-year recordkeeping, and run the written AML program (compliance officer, training, independent testing).
additions.supporting: SIU Investigator, Compliance Officer
additions.inputs: Escalated screening alerts, unusual transaction reports on cash-value products, KYC/source-of-funds information, AML program policies
additions.outputs: Filed SARs and OFAC blocked-property reports, blocked-account instructions, AML program testing and training records
additions.rationale: Verified: AML, KYC, SAR and FinCEN have zero hits in the model — RC-20-03-S01 lists 'suspicious activity' only as a generic input to regulator-engagement, which does not constitute the written AML program, alert investigation or SAR filing that 31 CFR 1025.210/.320 require of a carrier writing permanent life and annuities (SAR within 30 days of detection, 5-year retention). This is a hard federal obligation with criminal exposure; day-to-day investigation/filing sits with the financial-crime function inside this stream.

additions.name: Prepare & File ORSA Summary Report
additions.description: Annually consolidate the risk assessment, appetite, stress/scenario and prospective capital results into the Own Risk and Solvency Assessment, document the process, obtain CRO/board sign-off and file the confidential ORSA Summary Report with the lead state commissioner.
additions.supporting: Capital Model Actuary, Appointed Actuary, Chief Risk Officer
additions.inputs: Risk inventory and assessments, risk appetite, capital model and stress/scenario output, prior-year ORSA feedback
additions.outputs: Filed ORSA Summary Report, documented ERM self-assessment, board-reviewed prospective solvency view
additions.rationale: Verified: ORSA / 'own risk' has zero hits across the model. NAIC Model #505 (an accreditation standard) requires groups writing over $1B annual direct + assumed premium — which a combined P&C + Life group like Meridian exceeds — to conduct an ORSA at least annually and file the confidential Summary Report with the lead state commissioner. It is the capstone of exactly the ERM cycle RC-20-01 describes, slotting after Monitor Risks (S05) and before Report to Board (S06).

additions.name: Coordinate Market Conduct Exams & MCAS Filings
additions.description: Manage state DOI market conduct examinations end-to-end (exam call, data requests, interview logistics, response review, corrective-action commitments) and compile and submit the annual Market Conduct Annual Statement by the April 30 deadline for all applicable lines.
additions.supporting: Regulatory Affairs Manager, Compliance Analyst
additions.inputs: DOI exam calls and data requests, claims/underwriting/complaint practice data, MCAS blanks and instructions, prior exam findings
additions.outputs: Exam response packages, executed corrective-action plans, submitted MCAS filings
additions.deliverable: MCAS filing / market conduct exam response package
additions.rationale: Verified: market conduct and MCAS have zero hits in the model even though the role inventory contains a dedicated 'Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager' that leads nothing. MCAS is a mandatory annual NAIC filing (due April 30) for insurers writing at least $50,000 in an MCAS line per participating state, and market conduct exams under the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook are recurring, resource-intensive events that RC-20-03's five generic regulator-engagement steps do not capture; appending after S05 is correct.

additions.name: Log, Categorize & Approve Service Requests
additions.description: Receive standard IT service requests (software, hardware, information and standard pre-approved changes) through the service portal/catalog, categorize against the request catalog, obtain required business approvals, and route to the fulfillment group; access requests are routed to the identity-management flow (TR-25-02).
additions.supporting: IT Service Delivery Manager, Systems Administrator
additions.inputs: User requests via portal/catalog, request models and approval policies, request catalog definitions
additions.outputs: Categorized and approved request tickets, routing assignments, audit trail of approvals
additions.rationale: Verified: the stream covers ITIL event, incident, problem and release/hypercare practices, but service request management — a distinct ITIL 4 practice and the highest-volume service desk workload — has no home in any stream (OC-14/CI-04 'service request' hits are customer/policy servicing, not IT). The inventory's 'IT Service Desk Analyst' currently leads zero steps. Amended from the original proposal to scope out access requests, whose request/approve/provision lifecycle already exists at TR-25-02-S01..S03 in Cybersecurity, Identity & Resilience.

additions.name: Fulfill, Verify & Close Service Requests
additions.description: Execute the predefined fulfillment workflow (install software, deliver hardware, complete standard changes — access provisioning is executed in the TR-25-02 identity flow), verify completion with the requester, close the ticket, and report fulfillment SLA and automation metrics to drive catalog improvement.
additions.supporting: Systems Administrator, Network Administrator
additions.inputs: Approved request tickets, fulfillment runbooks and automation, asset and software deployment systems
additions.outputs: Fulfilled requests, requester confirmation, closed tickets, fulfillment SLA metrics
additions.rationale: Companion step completing the request lifecycle; ITIL 4 treats request fulfillment as a repeatable, often-automated workflow separate from incident restoration. Amended from the original proposal: access-provisioning execution (and its IAM Engineer / PAM Engineer role) was removed because TR-25-02-S03 'Provision Access' already covers it — this step handles the remaining catalog workload (software, hardware, standard changes) that the model otherwise omits entirely.

additions.name: Perform Clearance & Sanctions Screening
additions.description: Clear the logged submission against in-force and in-process accounts (duplicate submission and broker-of-record conflict check) and screen the insured, beneficial owners and key counterparties against OFAC SDN and other watchlists before any underwriting work begins; block and escalate hits to Compliance.
additions.supporting: Submission Intake Specialist, Compliance Analyst
additions.inputs: Logged submission, insured name/address/ownership data, in-force and in-process account records, OFAC SDN and watchlist data, broker-of-record records
additions.outputs: Clearance result (cleared / duplicate / BOR conflict), sanctions screening disposition, blocked-party escalation to Compliance
additions.rationale: Verified zero sanctions/OFAC/watchlist screening anywhere in all 29 streams (the only 'screen' hits are appetite, fraud and candidate screening), and no clearance/duplicate-submission check in intake. OFAC's 2024 insurance FAQs state a U.S. insurer is prohibited from issuing a policy to a blocked person and that underwriters are responsible for sanctions compliance throughout the policy lifecycle — screening at issuance is the minimum expectation, with documented checks re-run at bind. Submission clearance (duplicate/BOR check) is a universal commercial-lines intake step; binding two brokers' submissions for the same risk is a classic E&O failure. The 'Clearance Specialist' role exists in role-inventory.json but is used by zero steps, confirming the function was intended but never modeled.

additions.name: Confirm Reinsurance Capacity & Facultative Support
additions.description: Before final binding terms are agreed, verify the negotiated line fits within treaty capacity, limits and exclusions; where the risk exceeds automatic treaty capacity or falls in an excluded class, place facultative reinsurance and obtain reinsurer confirmation so the net retained position is approved prior to bind.
additions.supporting: Senior Underwriter, Ceded Reinsurance Analyst
additions.inputs: Negotiated terms, proposed line size, treaty capacity limits and exclusions, exposure schedules, facultative market quotes
additions.outputs: Treaty capacity confirmation, facultative placement confirmation (where required), net retention sign-off
additions.rationale: The current flow only notifies reinsurance AFTER bind (CI-06-04-S05 'Notify Billing & Reinsurance'), and the Reinsurance & Retrocession stream only identifies cession policies once bound (CI-05-03-S01) — verified no pre-bind capacity or facultative step anywhere. Facultative reinsurance is a discrete per-risk placement used precisely where treaty capacity is insufficient or the class is excluded, and must be quoted and confirmed before the cedant binds the primary risk; binding beyond treaty capacity without confirmed fac leaves the insurer unintentionally net — a finding any reinsurance auditor or rating agency would flag. The 'Facultative Reinsurance Specialist / Underwriter' role exists in the inventory but is used by zero steps. Inserted after Negotiate Terms (S04) so the net position is approved before Finalize Binding Terms (S05).

additions.name: Order & Evaluate Medical and Financial Evidence
additions.description: For life and annuity new business, order and evaluate underwriting evidence per age/amount requirements — MIB inquiry, prescription (Rx) and MVR database checks, paramedical exam, attending physician statements (APS) and financial questionnaires — then assign a risk class and render an approve/rate/decline decision.
additions.supporting: New Business Case Manager, Underwriting Assistant
additions.inputs: Life/annuity application, HIPAA and FCRA authorizations, MIB inquiry results, Rx and MVR reports, paramedical exam results, attending physician statements, financial questionnaires
additions.outputs: Evidence assessment, risk class assignment, underwriting decision (approve/rate/decline), requirements follow-up list
additions.rationale: Meridian is a combined P&C + Life & Retirement insurer, but the entire Submission-to-Bind stream is shaped around broker-submitted commercial P&C business (ACORD apps, loss runs, appetite triage, binders). Verified zero hits across all 29 streams for MIB, medical evidence, APS, paramedical or life new-business underwriting. MIB inquiry, Rx/MVR database checks, paramedical exams and APS ordered per age/amount grids are the standard life evidence workflow (FCRA-regulated consumer reports), culminating in risk-class assignment. The 'Life Underwriter' and 'New Business Case Manager' roles exist in the inventory with zero step usage, confirming the gap. Proposed as the first step of a new L4 under the existing Risk Assessment L3 since no existing L4 fits life new business.

additions.name: Review Replacement & Suitability
additions.description: Review annuity and life applications for replacement activity and best-interest/suitability compliance: validate replacement disclosure forms, assess the producer's recommendation against the consumer's profile per NAIC Model 275's care/disclosure/conflict/documentation obligations, and document the insurer's supervisory review before issue.
additions.supporting: New Business Case Manager, Compliance Analyst
additions.inputs: Application, replacement disclosure and comparison forms, consumer suitability/best-interest profile, producer recommendation documentation, existing-policy details
additions.outputs: Suitability determination, replacement compliance confirmation, documented basis of recommendation, declined/escalated cases
additions.rationale: Verified zero suitability/replacement/best-interest coverage across all 29 streams (the lone 'replacement' regex hit, CI-04-03-S05, is unrelated). NAIC Suitability in Annuity Transactions Model Regulation #275 (best-interest standard, now adopted in ~49 jurisdictions) explicitly requires the INSURER to establish and maintain a supervision system that reviews each recommendation so consumer needs are addressed before the annuity is issued, with heightened scrutiny for replacements/exchanges; state DOIs examine this directly. The 'Annuity Suitability Analyst' role exists in the inventory with zero step usage. Placed immediately after the medical/financial evidence step in the new Life & Annuity New Business Underwriting L4.

additions.l4: Performance, retention and org change support
additions.name: Process Offboarding & Access Revocation
additions.description: Execute the leaver process on resignation, termination or retirement: complete the exit checklist, conduct the exit interview, recover assets, trigger final pay and benefits continuation, and notify IAM same-day so all system, network and physical access is revoked with evidenced timestamps.
additions.supporting: Employee Relations Manager, IAM Analyst
additions.inputs: Resignation/termination notification, exit checklist template, asset and access inventory, final pay and benefits-continuation requirements
additions.outputs: Completed and signed exit checklist, access revocation confirmation with timestamps, asset return record, exit interview insights, final pay trigger
additions.rationale: The stream models hire-through-develop but has no leaver process anywhere: verified 'offboarding' exists only for vendors (Third-Party OC-13-04 'Risk remediation and offboarding'), and the Cybersecurity stream's 'Revoke/Modify Access' (TR-25-02-S05) has no HR-side trigger feeding it — so the access-revocation control exists elsewhere but the HR leaver event that initiates it is genuinely absent here. NIST SP 800-53 PS-4 requires disabling system access, revoking authenticators and retrieving property on termination, and ISO 27001 Annex A 6.5/5.18 require the same evidenced by termination-date-to-disablement-timestamp comparison; a former employee with live credentials is one of the most common IT/HR audit findings. Joiner-Mover-Leaver completeness is table stakes for a workforce value stream.

additions.name: Track Licensing & Continuing Education Compliance
additions.description: Maintain a register of employees in roles requiring state insurance licenses (claims adjusters, employee producers, customer-facing service staff), track license expirations and state CE requirements (typically 24 hours per biennium), assign and record CE coursework, and escalate lapsed or at-risk licenses to Compliance and the business.
additions.supporting: Producer Licensing Specialist, Compliance Analyst
additions.inputs: Roster of licensed/license-required roles, state licensing and CE requirements (NAIC SBS data), license expiry dates, CE course completions
additions.outputs: License and CE compliance register, renewal alerts, lapsed-license escalations, CE completion evidence
additions.rationale: Verified licensing is covered only for EXTERNAL parties: coverholders (CI-03-01-S02 'Verify Licensing & Credentials') and distribution producers (PG-16-02 partner enablement, PG-16-03-S02 'Onboard Producers') — the 'Producer Licensing Specialist' role is used only on those external-facing steps. Nothing tracks the insurer's own employees' licenses, yet most states license claims adjusters with ~24 CE hours every two years under the NAIC CE reciprocity agreement, and handling claims with an unlicensed adjuster is a direct market-conduct exam finding. This employee-capability obligation belongs in the workforce stream, distinct from the producer-licensing steps that already exist elsewhere.

additions.l4: Testing, deployment preparation and release control
additions.name: Conduct Security & Vulnerability Testing
additions.description: Run security verification on the release candidate before go-live: SAST/DAST and dependency scans in the pipeline, review against secure-coding standards and the threat model, penetration testing for high-risk changes, and disposition of vulnerability findings; security sign-off is a gate for the release recommendation.
additions.supporting: Security Analyst, Test Lead
additions.inputs: Build artifacts, SAST/DAST and dependency scan results, threat model, secure coding standards, penetration test scope for high-risk releases
additions.outputs: Security test report, vulnerability findings with remediation actions and risk acceptance decisions, security release sign-off
additions.rationale: Verified the delivery stream has zero security activity between requirements and production deployment (no security/vulnerability/penetration/SAST step anywhere in T-22), and the Cybersecurity stream covers security architecture (TR-25-01), IAM (TR-25-02), threat detection/response (TR-25-03) and resilience (TR-25-04) but no in-pipeline release security testing. NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.08 explicitly requires written procedures 'designed to ensure the use of secure development practices for in-house developed applications' and testing of externally developed applications, and Part 500 separately mandates risk-based penetration testing — an SDLC without a security gate is a direct Part 500 and SOX ITGC finding. The 'Application Security Lead' role exists in the inventory and is used only as Cybersecurity-stream support, never in delivery. Placed after Assess & Test (S03) so findings feed Document Findings and the go-live recommendation.

additions.name: Scan & Evaluate Emerging Technologies
additions.description: Continuously scan emerging technologies (AI, platforms, insurtech), assess relevance, risk and potential impact against capability gaps, run lightweight proof-of-concept evaluations, and classify candidates as adopt/trial/contain/hold to feed roadmap option development.
additions.supporting: Chief Technology Officer, Solution Architect, Data Science Lead
additions.inputs: Define Requirements results, analyst/vendor research, innovation proposals, capability gap analysis
additions.outputs: Emerging technology radar, PoC evaluation results, adopt/trial/contain/hold recommendations
additions.deliverable: Emerging technology radar with adopt/trial/hold recommendations
additions.rationale: COBIT 2019 APO04 (Managed Innovation) makes this a core management objective alongside strategy (APO02) and architecture (APO03): APO04.03 requires a technology-watch process scanning the external environment, APO04.04 requires assessing the business potential of emerging technologies, and APO04.05 requires evaluating proof-of-concept initiatives. Verified by full-text search of all 29 streams: no innovation, emerging-technology, proof-of-concept or pilot-evaluation step exists anywhere (the only 'emerging' hit is 'emerging and existing risks' in Risk & Compliance). For an insurer running AIOps/MLOps streams, a technology-strategy capability with no structured emerging-tech evaluation would be flagged in any COBIT or IT-strategy maturity assessment.
sources: ISACA COBIT 2019 Framework: Governance and Management Objectives (APO04.03-APO04.05)

additions.l4: Standards, reusable services and platform guardrails
additions.name: Maintain Technology Lifecycle & Obsolescence Roadmap
additions.description: Maintain the technology lifecycle register (emerging/standard/contain/retire) across applications, platforms and infrastructure; track vendor end-of-life/end-of-support dates against the asset inventory; and publish remediation/replacement plans for assets nearing obsolescence, escalating unsupported technology as risk acceptances.
additions.supporting: Platform Engineering Lead, Infrastructure / Network Engineer, IT Service Delivery Manager
additions.inputs: Asset/application inventory, vendor EOL/EOS notices, platform standards, technical debt register
additions.outputs: Technology lifecycle register, EOL remediation roadmap, replacement plans, risk acceptances for retained EOL assets
additions.deliverable: Technology lifecycle register and EOL remediation roadmap
additions.rationale: The FFIEC Architecture, Infrastructure & Operations booklet (Appendix A examination procedures) explicitly tests whether institutions identify and track assets' EOL time frames in inventories and develop replacement plans for assets nearing obsolescence; NYDFS Part 500 risk assessments likewise flag unsupported software. Verified by full-text search of all 29 streams: the only lifecycle reference is the phrase 'lifecycle decisions' in T-23-03-S05 outputs with no step that actually produces them — FinOps' 'decommission list' (T-27) is cloud rightsizing and MLOps lifecycle (TD-29) covers models only, and no asset-management/CMDB step exists anywhere else. This is the gap an examiner would flag first in this stream.

additions.name: Screen Vendor Against Sanctions & Watchlists
additions.description: Screen the vendor legal entity, principals and beneficial owners (OFAC 50% rule) against OFAC SDN, other sanctions lists and exclusion/debarment watchlists before contracting; adjudicate potential matches, escalate true matches to the financial crime team, and record the cleared-to-contract disposition. Re-screen on sanctions list updates.
additions.supporting: Financial Crime AML Officer, Third-Party Risk Manager
additions.inputs: Due diligence report, vendor legal entity details, beneficial ownership and principals, country/territory exposure
additions.outputs: Sanctions/watchlist screening result, match adjudication record, cleared-to-contract disposition
additions.deliverable: Vendor sanctions screening result and clearance disposition
additions.rationale: OFAC sanctions are strict liability — paying a blocked vendor is a violation regardless of intent — and OFAC's Framework for Compliance Commitments expects counterparty (including vendor) screening at onboarding and re-screening on list updates, since a vendor cleared at onboarding can be designated later. Verified by full-text search of the entire 29-stream model: ZERO occurrences of sanctions, OFAC, watchlist, SDN or denied-party screening anywhere (not in Risk & Compliance, claims payment, or underwriting), so this duplicates no control owned elsewhere; the vendor onboarding flow, after due diligence and before contracting, is the canonical place a TPRM examiner would look for it.
sources: OFAC, A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments (2019)

additions.name: Reassess Vendor Risk Tier & Recertify
additions.description: On a risk-based cycle (annual for critical vendors), refresh the vendor risk assessment beyond SLA performance: re-run due-diligence questionnaires, review financial health, cyber posture (SOC 2 / pen-test attestations), subcontractor changes and sanctions re-screening results; recertify or adjust the vendor risk tier and trigger enhanced monitoring or remediation (OC-13-04) where the profile has deteriorated.
additions.supporting: Vendor Manager, Compliance Analyst, Cybersecurity Lead
additions.inputs: Assess and Test results, refreshed due-diligence questionnaires, financial health and cyber posture attestations, sanctions re-screening results
additions.outputs: Refreshed vendor risk rating, recertification record, enhanced-monitoring or remediation triggers
additions.deliverable: Vendor risk recertification record with refreshed risk tier
additions.rationale: The 2023 Interagency TPRM Guidance's ongoing-monitoring stage and NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.11(a)(4) ('periodic assessment of such Third Party Service Providers based on the risk they present and the continued adequacy of their cybersecurity practices' — wording verified against the regulation text) both require periodic risk reassessment, not just SLA review. OC-13-03 today is purely SLA/performance and OC-13-04 only fires on audit findings/exit triggers; verified by model-wide search: no reassess/recertify step exists anywhere (the only periodic-review hit is TR-25-02-S04 'Certify Access', an IAM access certification, unrelated). This is among the most-cited TPRM exam findings for insurers.

additions.name: Verify Data Return, Destruction & Access Revocation
additions.description: Before exit closure, enforce the contract's data-handling clauses: obtain certificates of return or destruction for all customer NPI and company data held by the vendor, revoke all vendor network/system/badge access and service accounts (coordinating with IAM), recover assets, and retain the evidence pack as the offboarding control record.
additions.supporting: Vendor Manager, IAM Analyst, Data Protection Officer
additions.inputs: Validate and Control results, exit/transition plan, contract data-handling and destruction clauses, vendor access and data inventory
additions.outputs: Certificate of data destruction/return, access revocation confirmations, offboarding control evidence pack
additions.deliverable: Data destruction certificate and access revocation confirmation
additions.rationale: The termination stage of the 2023 Interagency TPRM lifecycle, the GLBA Safeguards Rule, and NYDFS third-party guidance on data exit obligations all expect verified return/destruction of customer information and prompt revocation of third-party access at relationship end; insurers are routinely cited when offboarded vendors retain data or live credentials. Verified by model-wide search: no 'data destruction', 'data return' or vendor access-revocation checkpoint exists anywhere in the 29 streams — TR-25-02-S05 (Revoke/Modify Access) is a generic IAM operation triggered by term/transfer notices, not a control gate inside the vendor exit flow, so this step invokes IAM rather than duplicating it.

modifications.rationale: Verified: outline uses 'Capital Modeling Actuary'/'Catastrophe (CAT) Modeler' on all five RF-21-03 steps while the inventory contains 'Capital Model Actuary' and 'CAT Modeler'. Role names must resolve against the 261-role inventory or role-based drill-downs and I/O resolution silently miss these steps.

modifications.issue: Supporting role 'Statutory Accountant' does not exist in role-inventory.json.
modifications.proposedFix: Replace with 'Statutory Reporting Analyst' (or 'Statutory Reporting Manager').
modifications.rationale: Verified absent from the inventory (which contains 'Statutory Reporting Analyst' and 'Statutory Reporting Manager'). Booking reserves into statutory financials is performed with the statutory reporting team; the current name will not resolve. Note the same phantom role also leads F-11-04-S06 in the Finance stream — out of scope here but worth flagging to that stream's owner.

modifications.issue: Supporting role 'CFO' is an abbreviation not present in role-inventory.json; similarly RF-21-02-S01 supporting includes 'Data Analyst', which is also not in the inventory.
modifications.proposedFix: S05: replace 'CFO' with 'Chief Financial Officer'. S01: replace 'Data Analyst' with 'Actuarial Technician' (or 'Data Engineer').
modifications.rationale: Verified: neither 'CFO' nor 'Data Analyst' appears in the inventory, breaking role-to-step resolution; the inventory contains 'Chief Financial Officer', 'Actuarial Technician' and 'Data Engineer' as canonical equivalents.

modifications.issue: The Appointed Actuary leads all five steps of routine portfolio performance monitoring and assumption refresh (RF-21-04-S01–S05).
modifications.proposedFix: Make 'Pricing Actuary' (or 'Reserving Actuary') the lead for day-to-day monitoring/assumption refresh, with 'Appointed Actuary' and 'Chief Actuary' supporting/reviewing.
modifications.rationale: The Appointed Actuary is a Board-appointed statutory officer responsible for the reserve opinion (NAIC Annual Statement Instructions), not the day-to-day operator of quarterly portfolio monitoring. Practitioners would also flag the independence optics of the opinion-signer owning the assumption refresh end-to-end.

modifications.issue: 'Premium Auditor' is the supporting role on every step of RC-19-01, RC-19-02 and RC-19-04. Premium audit is a policyholder exposure/payroll audit function within underwriting/billing operations — not internal audit staff.
modifications.proposedFix: Replace 'Premium Auditor' with 'Audit Associate' as the supporting role across RC-19-01, RC-19-02 and RC-19-04 (and add 'Audit Associate' to RC-19-03, which currently has supporting 'None').
modifications.rationale: Verified: 'Premium Auditor' supports all steps of RC-19-01/02/04 and RC-19-03 has supporting 'None'. Using a first-line operational role as internal audit engagement staff violates IIA independence/objectivity standards (Attribute Standards 1100/1120); the inventory already contains the correct 'Audit Associate' role.

modifications.issue: RC-19-01 (Risk-based audit planning) uses the fieldwork step template — 'Gather Evidence', 'Assess & Test', 'Document Findings', 'Report & Remediate' — even though the L4's output is an annual audit plan, not testing results.
modifications.proposedFix: Rename the planning steps to planning-appropriate verbs, e.g. S02 'Assess Audit Universe & Risks', S03 'Prioritize Engagements & Resources', S04 'Draft Annual Audit Plan', S05 'Publish Audit Plan & Schedule'.
modifications.rationale: Verified: RC-19-01 S01–S05 duplicate the exact fieldwork template used (correctly) in RC-19-02. IIA Standard 2010 planning produces a risk-based plan via risk assessment and prioritization; 'Assess & Test'/'Report & Remediate' describe engagement execution and will mislead anyone navigating the model.

modifications.issue: Supporting roles list both 'SRE' and 'Site Reliability Engineer' — the same role under two inventory aliases — on every step of TD-28-03 and TD-28-07.
modifications.proposedFix: Keep one ('SRE', the name used as lead elsewhere in this stream) and replace the duplicate with a genuinely distinct supporter, e.g. 'IT Service Delivery Manager' for TD-28-03 and 'Platform Engineering Lead' for TD-28-07.
modifications.rationale: Verified: the inventory contains both 'SRE' and 'Site Reliability Engineer' as separate entries, and all ten steps of TD-28-03/TD-28-07 list both as supporters. Duplicate-alias assignments inflate role-participation counts; the proposed replacements ('IT Service Delivery Manager', 'Platform Engineering Lead') both resolve in the inventory and match patterns used elsewhere in the stream.

modifications.issue: Step name 'Negotiate Settlement' is an exact duplicate of CI-02-04-S02 within the same L4 (verified in outline), making the two steps indistinguishable in role drill-downs, deliverable chains, and reporting.
modifications.proposedFix: Rename CI-02-04-S11 to 'Negotiate Pre-Trial Resolution' (its description is already 'Attempt pre-trial resolution'), keeping S02 as the primary claim-settlement negotiation step.
modifications.rationale: Two same-named steps in one L4 break unique step identification by name and confuse process consumers; the litigation-branch step is functionally distinct (mediation/pre-trial resolution under counsel).
sources: Standard BPM/APQC process-naming practice: unique activity names within a process scope

modifications.issue: 'Close Claim & Pursue Recoveries' sits at step 6, but the litigation sub-flow occupies steps 7-12 after it. As ordered, litigated claims are 'closed' before suit handling begins, and no closure step follows case resolution (S12 'Try or Settle Case' ends the L4 with the claim never closed). Verified in outline.
modifications.proposedFix: Reposition the litigation branch (current S07-S12) between S03 and the payment/closure steps, or renumber so 'Close Claim & Pursue Recoveries' is the final step of the L4 after 'Try or Settle Case', so every path (settled or litigated) terminates in payment and closure.
modifications.rationale: Industry claim lifecycle (intake → investigation → resolution [negotiated or litigated] → payment → recovery → closure) always ends with closure; a litigated claim resolved at trial still requires payment processing and file closure, which the current ordering never reaches.
sources: ACORD P&C claims capability model — claim lifecycle ends in settlement/closure

modifications.issue: Several SIU/litigation steps name roles that do not exist in role-inventory.json and so will not resolve in role drill-downs: 'Field Investigator' (CI-02-03-S09 supporting), 'Forensics Specialist' (CI-02-03-S10 supporting), 'SIU Manager' (CI-02-03-S08 supporting, S11 lead), 'Field Adjuster' (CI-02-03-S01 supporting), 'Outside Counsel' (CI-02-04-S09 supporting). All five verified absent from the 261-role inventory.
modifications.proposedFix: Map to inventory roles: Field Investigator/Forensics Specialist → 'SIU Investigator' (or add the specialist roles to the inventory); SIU Manager → 'SIU Investigator' lead with 'Claims Director / Manager' supporting; Field Adjuster → 'Claims Adjuster'; Outside Counsel → 'Litigation Counsel' supporting with 'Vendor Manager' for panel-firm management.
modifications.rationale: The platform resolves role-to-step links by name (no FK); steps naming non-inventory roles silently drop out of role views, understating SIU and litigation workload.
sources: Internal consistency check against role-inventory.json (261 roles)

modifications.issue: Stream-wide role-name drift from the inventory, all verified in the outline: 'Claims Intake Representative' vs inventory 'Claims Intake Rep'; 'Claims Adjuster / Examiner' vs 'Claims Adjuster'; 'Customer Service Representative' vs 'Customer Service Rep'; 'Chief Claims Officer (CCO)' vs 'Chief Claims Officer'.
modifications.proposedFix: Normalize all CI-02 step leads/supporting to the exact inventory strings ('Claims Intake Rep', 'Claims Adjuster', 'Customer Service Rep', 'Chief Claims Officer').
modifications.rationale: Name-based role resolution means these variants break every roles/deliverables drill-down for the highest-volume operational stream in the model.

modifications.issue: Steps across CI-01 reference 'Billing & Collections Manager' (verified at CI-01-01-S04/S05/S06, CI-01-03-S02/S05/S06, CI-01-04-S06), but the role inventory's entry is 'Billing Collections Manager' (no ampersand).
modifications.proposedFix: Normalize all occurrences to 'Billing Collections Manager' to match role-inventory.json.
modifications.rationale: Non-matching role string prevents the approval/oversight role for the whole billing stream from resolving in role-based views.

modifications.issue: Stream-wide role-name drift from the inventory, all verified in the outline: 'Program Management Office (PMO)' vs inventory 'Program Mgmt Office'; 'Learning & Development Manager' vs 'Learning Development Manager'; 'Release Train Engineer (RTE)' vs 'Release Train Engineer'.
modifications.proposedFix: Normalize all CS-07 step leads/supporting to the exact inventory strings ('Program Mgmt Office', 'Learning Development Manager', 'Release Train Engineer').
modifications.rationale: Every step in this stream names at least one non-resolving role, so the stream contributes nothing to role drill-downs despite being fully populated.

modifications.issue: The 'Communications and training preparation' L4 (CS-07-02) names only Learning & Development Manager and Organizational Change Manager; no communications role participates even though the L4's final outputs include the comms calendar (verified at CS-07-02-S05).
modifications.proposedFix: Add 'Communications Specialist' as a supporting role on CS-07-02 steps (at minimum S03 Execute & Process and S05 Finalize & Handoff).
modifications.rationale: Prosci's communications plan is one of the five core change levers and is normally produced by communications professionals, not L&D; the inventory contains the role but it is unused in the one L4 that owns communications outputs.

modifications.issue: All five steps of 'Recovery collection, settlement and closeout' are led by 'Reinsurance Claims / Recoveries Specialist', but this L4 is direct subrogation/third-party recovery collection. Reinsurance recoverables are already owned end-to-end by CI-05-04 (Reinsurance & Retrocession Management), where Reinsurance Analyst/Manager bill and collect from reinsurers.
modifications.proposedFix: Change leads on CI-26-04-S01 through S05 to 'Collections Recovery Specialist' (or 'Subrogation Specialist'), keeping 'Subrogation / Litigation Specialist' as supporting.
modifications.rationale: Direct subrogation collection (demands on adverse carriers/parties, payment plans, intercompany arbitration awards) is performed by subrogation/collections staff, not the reinsurance recoverables team; the current assignment conflates two distinct recovery flows that the model otherwise correctly separates (verified: CI-05-04 steps S01-S06 already cover tracking recoverable balances, billing reinsurers and collections under Reinsurance Analyst/Manager).

modifications.issue: 'Receive Customer Contact' (accept inbound inquiry via any channel) duplicates the entire OC-14-01 L4 'Contact intake and case routing', whose output is already a 'logged interaction, routed case'. The resolution L4 re-performs intake instead of consuming the routed case.
modifications.proposedFix: Rename/redefine OC-14-02-S01 as 'Review Routed Case & Confirm Scope' with inputs 'Routed case, service priority (from OC-14-01)' and output 'Confirmed service request'.
modifications.rationale: Industry contact-center reference models (intake/route then resolve) keep channel intake in one place; the duplication creates two competing systems of record for the same interaction and breaks the L4-to-L4 handoff the outline itself defines (OC-14-01-S05 outputs 'Logged interaction, routed case, service priority').

modifications.issue: Roles across OC-14-01 (S01–S05) and OC-14-02 (S01–S06) are not in the role inventory: 'Customer Service Representative (CSR)', 'Customer Service Representative', 'Contact Center Operations Manager', 'Contact Center Supervisor', 'Subject Matter Expert', 'Claims/Billing/UW Specialist', 'Quality Analyst', 'Customer Experience Manager'.
modifications.proposedFix: Map to inventory names: 'Customer Service Rep' (leads), 'Contact Center Ops Manager' (supervisor/ops manager), 'Senior Contact Center Agent' (escalation), 'Quality Assurance Analyst (Service)' (QA), 'Customer Experience Lead' (CX), and concrete specialists ('Claims Analyst', 'Billing Analyst', 'Underwriting Assistant') instead of 'Claims/Billing/UW Specialist' and 'Subject Matter Expert'.
modifications.rationale: Verified: all eight off-inventory names appear verbatim in the outline and none exist in role-inventory.json, while every proposed replacement does. Steps whose leads/supporting are free-text variants break the role-resolution chain (deliverables/tasks resolve by exact role-name match), so these steps will show no owners in role drill-downs and workforce analytics.

modifications.issue: All five steps of 'Security architecture and control definition' use 'ISO Security Architect' (lead) and 'Chief Information Security Officer' (supporting), neither of which is in the role inventory; the inventory has 'ISO Architect' and 'Chief Info Security Officer'.
modifications.proposedFix: Change leads on TR-25-01-S01 through S05 to 'ISO Architect' and supporting to 'Application Security Lead, Chief Info Security Officer'.
modifications.rationale: Verified: the outline uses 'ISO Security Architect'/'Chief Information Security Officer' on TR-25-01-S01..S05 and the inventory contains only 'ISO Architect'/'Chief Info Security Officer'. Near-miss role names silently orphan the steps from role-based views; exact inventory names restore the linkage with no semantic change.

modifications.issue: The IAM L4 uses roles not in the inventory: 'Requesting Manager' (S01 lead), 'Data Owner' (S02/S04 lead), 'IT Support' (S03 supporting), 'Internal Auditor' (S06 lead).
modifications.proposedFix: Map to inventory roles: 'Operations Manager' or 'HR Business Partner' for the requesting line manager, 'Data Steward' for Data Owner, 'IT Service Desk Analyst' for IT Support, 'Internal Audit' for Internal Auditor.
modifications.rationale: The process logic (request → approve → provision → certify → revoke → audit) is sound and matches SOX/NYDFS access-control expectations, but the actor names must resolve against the 261-role inventory for the model to be usable in role drill-downs and access-review accountability reporting; all four off-inventory names verified present in TR-25-02 and all replacements verified in the inventory.

modifications.issue: 'SOC Analyst' (lead on S01/S02, supporting on S03) and 'IT Operations' (supporting on S04) are not in the role inventory; the inventory has 'Security Analyst', 'SOC Lead', and infrastructure roles.
modifications.proposedFix: Replace 'SOC Analyst' with 'Security Analyst' and 'IT Operations' with 'Infrastructure / Network Engineer' (or 'IT Service Delivery Manager') on TR-25-03-S01 through S04.
modifications.rationale: Same role-resolution defect as above: the SOC monitoring/triage steps will not surface under any real role, which understates the Security Analyst workload in the operating model; off-inventory names verified present in TR-25-03 and replacements verified in the inventory.

modifications.issue: The Chief Data Officer is named day-to-day lead of all five Data Product Intake steps (S01–S05), including Build & Configure — an executive cannot be the operational lead for requirements capture and build work. Verified in outline: CDO is lead on every TD-24-01 step.
modifications.proposedFix: Make Data Architect the lead for S01–S04 (supporting: Data Steward, BI / Analytics Manager), reserving Chief Data Officer as lead/approver only on S05 Approve & Publish.
modifications.rationale: Operating models distinguish accountable executives from process operators; CDO-as-lead on every step makes the RACI unusable for staffing and contradicts how the other TD-24 L4s assign working-level leads (Data Quality Manager, Data Steward). All replacement roles verified in role-inventory.json.

modifications.issue: Supporting role 'Business Unit Heads' is not in the 261-role inventory; the same defect recurs in this L4: S03 supporting 'Data Analyst', S04 supporting 'Business SME', S06 supporting 'Data Governance Committee' — none are inventory roles (all four absences verified against role-inventory.json).
modifications.proposedFix: S02 supporting → 'Data Governance, Data Steward'; S03 supporting → 'Data Steward, BI / Analytics Manager'; S04 supporting → 'Data Engineer, Data Steward'; S06 supporting → 'Data Governance'.
modifications.rationale: Role-resolved views (deliverable→role→task chains) silently drop steps whose roles do not match the inventory; the inventory already contains the correct equivalents ('Data Governance' is a named role).

modifications.issue: 'Verify Licensing & Credentials' checks licenses only (inputs: 'Licensing status, state requirements'; outputs: 'License verification report'); professional indemnity (E&O) cover and premium trust/bank account details — mandatory items in Lloyd's coverholder due diligence and annual compliance — are absent from inputs and outputs.
modifications.proposedFix: Extend inputs to 'Licensing status, state requirements, E&O/professional indemnity certificates, premium trust account details' and outputs to 'License verification report, E&O cover confirmation, bank/trust account verification'.
modifications.rationale: Lloyd's coverholder approval and annual compliance explicitly cover professional indemnity, licences, financials and bank accounts; an authority granted to a partner with lapsed PI cover is a material E&O and regulatory exposure.

modifications.issue: Routine, ongoing control testing within Operational Oversight is led by 'Internal Auditor' — a role not in the inventory ('Internal Audit' is the inventory name; absence verified) — and assigning internal audit as first-line operator of a recurring control conflicts with IIA Three Lines independence, since the same function then audits this activity in CI-03-04-S01.
modifications.proposedFix: Lead → 'Delegated Authority Analyst' (inventory role), supporting → 'Compliance Analyst, Delegated Authority Manager'; reserve 'Internal Audit' for the periodic audit steps in CI-03-04 (and correct the 'Internal Auditor' spelling there and in CI-03-02-S03 supporting).
modifications.rationale: Under the IIA Three Lines Model, management (first line) performs day-to-day control monitoring and internal audit (third line) provides independent periodic assurance; the current assignment destroys audit independence over delegated authority oversight.

modifications.issue: Lead 'Data Analyst' is not in the role inventory (verified), while the inventory contains the purpose-built 'Bordereaux Analyst' role that exists precisely for bordereaux validation; same substitution applies to the 'Data Analyst' supporting entries in CI-03-03-S01 and CI-03-02-S04 (both verified present in the outline).
modifications.proposedFix: Replace 'Data Analyst' with 'Bordereaux Analyst' as lead of S02 and as supporting in CI-03-03-S01 and CI-03-02-S04.
modifications.rationale: Bordereaux validation is the defining task of the Bordereaux Analyst role in the inventory; using a non-inventory generic role breaks role-resolved navigation and orphans the real role.
sources: Lloyd's delegated authority reporting standards (Coverholder Reporting Standards v5)

modifications.issue: 'Onboard Producers' (S02) and 'Train on Products' (S03) inside Pipeline Development duplicate the entire PG-16-02 Partner Enablement L4 ('Broker/MGA onboarding and enablement' — whose outputs already include onboarded partner, enablement pack, training and access setup; duplication verified in the outline), creating two competing onboarding flows with no handoff between them.
modifications.proposedFix: Refocus PG-16-03 on pipeline activities (recruit → set goals → activate → monitor → compensate) and route recruited producers into PG-16-02 for contracting, setup and training: replace S02 with a handoff step 'Refer Producer to Onboarding (PG-16-02)' or fold S02/S03 content into PG-16-02 and renumber.
modifications.rationale: Duplicate onboarding paths mean the regulatory controls added to PG-16-02 (screening, appointments) can be bypassed via the PG-16-03 path; a single producer-lifecycle flow is the industry norm in producer management platforms.

modifications.issue: PG-16-03 is saturated with roles absent from the inventory (all verified): S06 lead 'Producer Relations Manager' and supporting 'Commissions Analyst, AP Specialist'; S01 lead 'Business Development Manager' and supporting 'Territory Manager'/'Marketing Manager'; S02 'IT Support'; S03 'Training Manager'/'Product Manager'; S04 lead 'Territory Manager' and supporting 'Business Development Manager'; S05 lead 'Territory Manager' and supporting 'Producer Relations Manager'.
modifications.proposedFix: Map to inventory roles: S06 lead → 'Commission Analyst', supporting → 'Distribution Operations Manager, Channel Operations Coordinator'; 'Producer Relations Manager' → 'Agency Relations Manager'; 'Business Development Manager' → 'Business Dev Manager' (exact inventory spelling); 'Territory Manager' → 'Sales / Distribution Analyst' or 'Business Dev Manager'; 'Marketing Manager' → 'Marketing Coordinator'; 'Training Manager' → 'Training Coordinator'; 'Product Manager' → 'Insurance Product Manager'; 'IT Support' → 'IT Service Desk Analyst'.
modifications.rationale: Every step in this L4 fails role-inventory validation, so the whole Pipeline Development sub-process disappears from role-based views and staffing analyses; the inventory contains direct equivalents for each role (all proposed replacements verified present in role-inventory.json).

modifications.issue: Step 'Manage Liquidity' (inputs: cash flows/investments; output: liquidity position) duplicates the entire F-11-03 L4 'Cash, liquidity and funding management' (whose S05 already outputs 'Liquidity plan, funding actions, cash positioning') and is off-topic inside an L4 named 'Capital actions, tax and solvency reporting'. Meanwhile no step in F-11-04 actually executes capital actions, which the L4 name promises.
modifications.proposedFix: Replace with 'Execute Capital Actions': plan and execute shareholder/parent dividends (including 30-day prior notice or approval for extraordinary dividends under the state Holding Company Act), capital contributions and surplus notes. Lead: Treasury Manager; supporting: Capital Management Manager, Chief Financial Officer.
modifications.rationale: Duplication verified against the outline: F-11-03-S05 and F-11-04-S05 both own the liquidity-position output. NAIC Insurance Holding Company System Regulatory Act (Model #440) requires commissioner notice/approval for extraordinary dividends and reporting of all dividends — a regulated capital-action process every US insurer must run, currently absent. All three replacement roles are exact role-inventory names.

modifications.issue: Lead 'Statutory Accountant' is not in the 261-role inventory (verified: also used as lead on F-11-04-S06 and supporting on F-11-01-S04). Role resolution (roleMatch on leads/supporting) will fail for these steps.
modifications.proposedFix: Use 'Statutory Reporting Analyst' as lead (preparer) with 'Statutory Reporting Manager' supporting on F-11-01-S04, F-11-01-S06 and F-11-04-S06.
modifications.rationale: Both statutory reporting roles exist exactly in role-inventory.json; the invented 'Statutory Accountant' breaks the role-to-step linkage the platform resolves at query time. All three cited step codes verified present in the outline with the bad role string.
sources: role-inventory.json (Statutory Reporting Analyst / Statutory Reporting Manager)

modifications.issue: Lead 'Department Managers' is a generic placeholder, not a role in the inventory; the step has no resolvable owner (verified in outline).
modifications.proposedFix: Lead: 'FP&A Manager' (facilitates and owns the bottoms-up budget build); supporting: 'Operations Manager, Financial Analyst' as the cost-center-owner representatives.
modifications.rationale: Every L5 step must resolve to inventory roles for the deliverable/role/task chain to work; 'FP&A Manager', 'Operations Manager' and 'Financial Analyst' are all exact inventory names, and FP&A facilitating department budget builds matches standard FP&A operating practice.

modifications.issue: Lead 'CEO' and supporting 'CFO, Board of Directors' are not in the role inventory (verified; likewise 'CEO, Business Unit Heads' on F-11-02-S05, 'BU Heads' on F-11-04-S03, and bare 'CFO' on F-11-01-S05, F-11-02-S01/S05 and F-11-04-S01/S03/S04/S05 vs the inventory's 'Chief Financial Officer').
modifications.proposedFix: Replace shorthand with canonical inventory names across F-11: lead F-11-02-S06 = 'Chief Financial Officer', supporting 'Chief Operating Officer, Board Governance Lead'; replace 'BU Heads'/'Business Unit Heads' with 'Chief Underwriting Officer, Chief Operating Officer'; replace bare 'CFO' with 'Chief Financial Officer'.
modifications.rationale: These steps use free-text executive shorthand that breaks role resolution; there is no 'CEO' or 'Board of Directors' role in the inventory — 'Board Governance Lead' is the inventory's board-facing role (it already leads EM-10-04). All replacement names verified as exact inventory strings.

modifications.issue: The Chief Product Officer is the day-to-day lead of all five demand-shaping/prioritization steps (S01–S05, verified). Intake, scoring and sequencing are operational portfolio activities; a C-suite officer is the decision-maker, not the step operator.
modifications.proposedFix: Lead: 'Program Mgmt Office' for S01–S05 (portfolio operations function per SAFe LPM), with 'Chief Product Officer, Chief Technology Officer, Chief Operating Officer' as supporting decision-makers.
modifications.rationale: SAFe Lean Portfolio Management assigns portfolio operations (intake, WSJF scoring, Kanban management, sync facilitation) to the ePMO/VMO, with executives participating in the decision forums; modeling executives as operators distorts workload and RACI views the platform derives from leads. Supporting names amended to exact inventory strings ('Chief Operating Officer', not 'Chief Operating Officer (COO)').

modifications.issue: L4 'Commitment & rate optimization (RIs/Savings Plans)' uses the incident-response step template (Detect & Log → Triage & Assign → Investigate & Act → Resolve & Verify → Close & Report), verified in the outline. Commitment purchasing is a deliberate planning/decision cycle, not an event-driven flow, and the template hides the required financial-approval gate before multi-year spend commitments.
modifications.proposedFix: Rename the five steps to a decision-cycle pattern: Analyze Usage & Coverage → Model Commitment Options → Approve Commitment Purchase (Finance/Treasury sign-off) → Execute Purchase → Track Coverage & Utilization. Keep existing leads (FinOps Lead) with Treasury Manager supporting the approval step.
modifications.rationale: FinOps Foundation Rate Optimization capability describes an analyze-recommend-approve-purchase-track cadence; reserved instances and savings plans are 1–3 year financial obligations, so the approval gate is a control a CFO organization would expect to see named explicitly. Treasury Manager already appears as supporting on this L4, so the fix requires no new role wiring.

modifications.issue: L4 F-12-04 is titled 'Portfolio monitoring and investment reporting' (L3 Performance & Risk Reporting) but its steps S01-S04 are actually policy setting, opportunity analysis, trade execution, and settlement. S01 'Set Investment Policy' duplicates F-12-01, whose finalized output is already 'Investment policy, allocation targets, mandate constraints, performance objectives'; S02 'Analyze Opportunities' overlaps F-12-02 security selection.
modifications.proposedFix: Remove S01 (consume 'Investment policy' from F-12-01's output as an input instead) and retitle the L4 to 'Trade execution, settlement, valuation and investment reporting' so the execution/settlement steps it uniquely contains are honestly labeled; alternatively move S02 into F-12-02.
modifications.rationale: Trade execution and settlement exist nowhere else in the model, so they must stay — but a duplicated policy-setting step creates two competing sources for the same governing document, and the current L4/L3 naming hides the model's only execution-and-settlement flow under a 'reporting' label. Verified in the outline: F-12-01-S05 already outputs the investment policy that F-12-04-S01 re-creates.

modifications.issue: Lead 'Chief Investment Officer (CIO)' does not match any role-inventory name (inventory has 'Chief Investment Officer'); the same invalid token is used on every step of F-12-01 (lead), F-12-02 (supporting), and F-12-03 (lead) — verified on all 15 steps.
modifications.proposedFix: Normalize the role to 'Chief Investment Officer' across F-12-01-S01..S05, F-12-02-S01..S05 (supporting), and F-12-03-S01..S05.
modifications.rationale: Role names that don't match the inventory break role-based drill-downs and RACI reporting; this is a data-fidelity defect, not a stylistic choice.

modifications.issue: Lead 'CFO' and supporting 'Board' are not role-inventory names ('CFO' should be 'Chief Financial Officer'; 'Board' is a governance body, not a role).
modifications.proposedFix: If F-12-04-S01 is retained (the companion logic fix proposes removing it as a duplicate of F-12-01): lead = 'Chief Financial Officer'; supporting = 'Chief Investment Officer, Board Governance Lead' (the Board Governance Lead carries the board-approval interaction). If S01 is removed, this fix is moot.
modifications.rationale: Invalid role tokens orphan the step from the role model; board approval of the investment policy is required under the NAIC investment model acts, so the board interface should map to a real role.

modifications.issue: Supporting includes 'Trader', which is not in the role inventory.
modifications.proposedFix: Supporting = 'Portfolio Manager, Chief Investment Officer' (or add a Trader/Execution role to the inventory if a dealing desk genuinely exists at Meridian).
modifications.rationale: Every step role must resolve to the 261-role inventory; Portfolio Manager is the closest practitioner who places orders in the current model.

modifications.issue: Supporting 'Custodian' is an external counterparty (custodian bank), not an internal role, and is not in the role inventory.
modifications.proposedFix: Supporting = 'Investment Operations Manager' (who manages the custodian interface); reference the custodian bank in inputs ('custodian confirmations') rather than as a role.
modifications.rationale: External parties belong in inputs/outputs, not the RACI; Investment Operations Manager is the inventory role that owns settlement and custody interaction day-to-day, and also leads the proposed custody-reconciliation step that follows S04.

modifications.issue: Supporting 'Statutory Accountant' is not in the role inventory.
modifications.proposedFix: Supporting = 'Statutory Reporting Analyst, Senior Accountant'.
modifications.rationale: Direct inventory equivalents exist; statutory valuation (amortized cost vs fair value by NAIC designation) is exactly the Statutory Reporting Analyst's remit. (Note: the same invalid 'Statutory Accountant' token also appears outside this stream as lead of F-11-01-S06 — worth a follow-up sweep.)

modifications.issue: Lead 'Business Requestor' is not a role in the inventory — it is a placeholder for whoever submits the request (it also appears as supporting on CS-08-02-S03).
modifications.proposedFix: Lead = 'Contract Administrator' (intake owner of contract requests); supporting = 'Contracts Manager'. The requesting business unit is captured in inputs, not as a role.
modifications.rationale: A step cannot be led by an undefined placeholder; Contract Administrator exists in the inventory and is the standard intake role in a contract lifecycle process.

modifications.issue: Lead 'Legal Counsel' (also supporting on S02) is not an inventory role — the inventory only has specialized counsel roles (Coverage, Litigation, Privacy, Regulatory) and General Counsel.

modifications.issue: L4 CI-04-04 'Complaint intake, investigation and response' (lead: Complaints Manager) substantially duplicates OC-14-03 'Formal complaint handling and regulatory response' in the Customer Service, Complaints & Experience stream (verified: both exist and both are led by Complaints Manager) — two parallel end-to-end complaint processes with no stated scope boundary or handoff.
modifications.proposedFix: Scope CI-04-04 to first-tier servicing complaints arising from policy admin transactions, with an explicit escalation output/handoff to OC-14-03 for formal/DOI complaints (add 'escalation to formal complaint process (OC-14-03)' to CI-04-04-S05 outputs and rename the L4 'Servicing complaint triage and first-tier resolution'); keep regulator-facing response solely in OC-14-03.
modifications.rationale: Regulators require a single auditable complaint register and response process (NAIC market conduct annual statement complaint reporting); duplicated ownership across streams risks double-counting or dropped DOI deadlines.

modifications.issue: Step 5 'File Rate/Form Changes' outputs only 'Regulatory filings', and step 6 'Implement Changes' takes 'Approved changes' as input — but no step captures regulator objection handling/approval between filing and implementation; in prior-approval states implementing before approval is a compliance violation.

modifications.rationale: The I/O chain currently breaks: 'Approved changes' appears as an input with no producing step. PG-18-02-S06 handles approval management for new products ('File with state regulators and manage approval'), so the iteration L4 should mirror it. (Amended from the original proposal: stepCode retargeted from S06 to S05 — the step actually being changed — and reclassified from 'ordering' to 'io' since no reordering is proposed.)

modifications.issue: Steps S07–S12 of RC-20-02 ('Develop Audit Plan' through 'Track Remediation') embed the complete internal audit lifecycle inside the compliance 'Control Monitoring' L4, duplicating the dedicated Audit & Assurance stream (verified present: RC-19-01 Audit Planning, RC-19-02 Fieldwork & Testing, RC-19-03 Reporting, RC-19-04 Issue Follow-up). The duplicated steps also use non-inventory role strings ('Chief Audit Executive', 'Audit Staff', 'Auditee Mgmt', 'Auditee Management').

modifications.rationale: Internal audit is the third line and must be organizationally independent of the compliance (second-line) function per the IIA Three Lines Model; modeling audit planning/fieldwork/reporting inside compliance control monitoring both duplicates RC-19 and misstates the independence a regulator or external QA review would test. Removal also eliminates four non-inventory role strings.

modifications.issue: 'Complete Pre-Employment' describes only generic 'background and pre-hire processing' with output 'Cleared candidate'. It omits the insurance-specific 18 U.S.C. §1033 prohibited-persons screening: insurers are federally barred from permitting anyone convicted of a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust to engage in the business of insurance without written regulator consent (a 1033 waiver), with civil penalties up to $50,000 per occurrence.
modifications.proposedFix: Expand the step description and outputs to include §1033 prohibited-persons screening and waiver routing: outputs become 'Cleared candidate, §1033 attestation/screening result, waiver application where required'; supporting roles add 'Compliance Analyst'.
modifications.rationale: This is the single most distinctive regulatory control in insurer hiring — §1033 prohibits insurers from willfully permitting prohibited persons to participate in the business of insurance, so the obligation sits with the employer's pre-hire screening, and a market-conduct or internal-audit review would flag its absence. Modeling it inside the existing pre-employment step is better than a new step.

modifications.issue: Several role names in this stream do not exist in the 261-role inventory: 'Compensation & Benefits Manager' (supporting on all CS-09-01 steps; inventory name is 'Comp Benefits Manager'), 'Learning & Development Manager' (lead on all CS-09-03 steps; inventory name is 'Learning Development Manager'), 'Training Manager' (CS-09-02-S06 supporting; nearest inventory role 'Training Coordinator'), and 'Hiring Manager'/'Interview Panel' (CS-09-02-S01/S03/S04/S06) which have no inventory entry at all.

For 'Hiring Manager'/'Interview Panel', either add a generic line-manager role to the inventory or re-lead those steps with 'HR Business Partner'/'Recruiter' and note the hiring manager in the description.
modifications.rationale: Verified every flagged name is absent from role-inventory.json and every proposed target is present exactly; near-miss spellings ('&' variants) break exact role matching used for role drill-downs, and steps led by roles outside the inventory orphan their deliverables from every role view.

modifications.issue: 'Deploy to Production' sits at the end of the Build & Integration L4 (T-22-02), which means production deployment occurs BEFORE the Quality & Release L4 (T-22-03) and entirely bypasses the Deployment & Change Control L4 (T-22-04) with its CAB approval, deployment preparation and rollback planning. As sequenced, code reaches production twice — once unguarded at T-22-02-S06 and again under change control at T-22-04-S05.
modifications.proposedFix: Rename T-22-02-S06 to 'Promote to Test/Staging Environment' with output 'Release candidate handed to T-22-03 Quality & Release'; production deployment should occur only via T-22-04-S04/S05 after CAB approval.
modifications.rationale: Verified the sequencing in the outline: T-22-02-S06 outputs 'Production release' while T-22-04-S03/S05 separately perform CAB approval and 'Implement change in production'. ITIL change enablement and SOX ITGC require that all production changes pass release verification and authorized change control; an uncontrolled production-deploy path inside the build phase is a textbook ITGC deficiency.

modifications.issue: 'Initiate Project' takes input 'Business requirements' and S02 'Gather Requirements' re-elicits requirements, ignoring that the Demand & Analysis L4 (T-22-01-S05) already hands off 'Prioritized backlog, requirements, scope statement, dependency list'. The two L4s are disconnected and duplicate requirements work.
modifications.proposedFix: Change T-22-02-S01 inputs to 'Prioritized backlog, requirements, scope statement, dependency list (from T-22-01)'; scope S02 to 'detail/refine requirements into specifications' rather than re-gathering them.
modifications.rationale: Verified T-22-01-S05's outputs ('Prioritized backlog, requirements, scope statement, dependency list') feed nothing downstream while T-22-02-S01 starts from generic 'Business requirements'. The deliverable chain should connect L4 to L4; as written the demand stage's outputs are orphaned, which the sidebar deliverable-chain view will expose as a broken handoff.

modifications.issue: 'Verify & Close' takes input 'Test results' (a pre-release artifact from T-22-03) rather than the post-deployment validation evidence produced by T-22-04-S05 'Execute Change' (output 'Implemented change'). It also closes the change with no post-implementation review, which ITIL requires for major, emergency and failed changes.
modifications.proposedFix: Change inputs to 'Implemented change, post-deployment validation and monitoring results'; expand the step to 'Verify, Review & Close' with outputs 'Closed change, post-implementation review findings, CMDB update'.
modifications.rationale: Verified in the outline that T-22-04-S06's input is 'Test results' while its predecessor S05 outputs 'Implemented change'. Verification of a production change must consume evidence from the production environment, not earlier test-cycle results; PIR closure is the standard ITIL/CAB feedback loop auditors look for.

modifications.rationale: Verified all flagged names are absent from role-inventory.json and all proposed targets ('Change Coordinator', 'DevOps / Platform Automation Engineer', 'Technical Project Manager', 'IT Service Delivery Manager', 'Head of IT') are present exactly; group placeholders and near-miss titles orphan these steps from every role view.

modifications.issue: The L4 'Standards, reusable services and platform guardrails' (T-23-03) uses the incident/case-handling template (Detect & Log → Triage & Assign → Investigate & Act → Resolve & Verify → Close & Report) for what is a definitional, publish-and-govern process. Defining platform standards and guardrails is not triggered by detected events, and 'Detect & Log' makes no sense as the first step of authoring standards. Verified in the outline: S02 desc is 'Triage severity and assign ownership' yet S05 outputs are 'Platform standards, guardrails, reusable patterns, lifecycle decisions'.
modifications.proposedFix: Re-template T-23-03 steps to the definitional flow used by its sibling L4s T-23-01/T-23-02: Define Requirements → Develop Approach → Build & Configure → Validate & Review → Approve & Publish, keeping the existing leads (Platform Engineering Lead), supporting roles (DBA, Site Reliability Engineer), the existing S01 inputs (architecture decisions, service standards, operational constraints, risk controls) and the existing S05 outputs (platform standards, guardrails, reusable patterns, lifecycle decisions).
modifications.rationale: TOGAF's standards/architecture content lifecycle and COBIT APO03 treat standards definition as a develop-review-approve-publish cycle, not detect-triage-resolve. The mismatch breaks the inputs/outputs chain semantics and would confuse any practitioner walking the model; both sibling L4s in the same stream already use the correct template.

modifications.issue: OC-13-01 'Vendor demand intake and selection' overruns its scope: S03 (Negotiate Contract) and S04 (Execute Contract) duplicate OC-13-02 'Risk review and contract finalization' (whose S05 output is verified as 'Approved vendor pack, negotiated contract, control requirements, onboarding conditions'), and S06 (Monitor Performance — 'Track vendor delivery and SLAs') duplicates the entire OC-13-03 'Service review and SLA governance' L4. The same contract is negotiated/finalized in two L4s and SLA monitoring lives in two places.
modifications.proposedFix: End OC-13-01 at selection and onboarding: keep S01 (Identify Vendor Need), S02 (Conduct Due Diligence), the new sanctions-screening step, and S05 (Onboard Vendor, renumbered after contract execution in OC-13-02); move/merge S03-S04 contracting outputs into OC-13-02 as the single contracting home; delete S06 and hand off to OC-13-03 via an explicit output ('vendor setup complete, monitoring handover to service review').
modifications.rationale: The 2023 Interagency TPRM Guidance defines discrete lifecycle stages — planning, due diligence & selection, contract negotiation, ongoing monitoring, termination — and the model's own L3s mirror them (Vendor Sourcing / Due Diligence & Contracting / Performance Management / Risk & Exit Management). Having sourcing also perform contracting and monitoring breaks the stage boundaries, double-counts the deliverable chain, and creates ambiguous ownership between Vendor Manager and Contracts Manager.
